stories.title: Thai woman pleads with husband:'No money even for food; return ₹60 lakh', Kanpur’s Irfan remarried by lying
stories.summary: An audio recording has emerged of a woman from Thailand who accused a Kanpur businessman of marrying her for a second time by lying to her. In the recording, she can be heard pleading with the businessman, Irfan. She says, ‘My financial situation is very bad. I do not even have money for food. You have a family, but I have no one here. Return my ₹60 lakh.’ Irfan then begins arguing with her. He says, ‘I am also very troubled. I am not lying. I will return the money as soon as I receive payment from the customer.’ In the recording, Irfan can also be heard evading the conversation by citing that his bank account is frozen and saying that he is at the police station. In fact, the Thai woman, Apsorn, suddenly arrived in Kanpur on Tuesday and complained to the ADCP that she had been defrauded. She said the accused had married her by lying to her and then defrauded her of ₹60 lakh. He was now distancing himself from her. The woman also accused the man of pressuring her to convert to Islam forcibly. The police subsequently arrested the accused and sent him to jail. WhatsApp call recordings and chats handed over to police Read the WhatsApp chat between Irfan and Apsorn Irfan: Everything is about the same thing again... You only think about money in every matter. You do not think about anything else. Apsorn: My life is in a very difficult situation. I have to make payments every day. I do not even have money to buy food. You have a family, but I have no one here. Irfan: I have a lot of problems too. You do not listen to me either because you are angry. Apsorn: When I message you, you do not reply. But you have time to message your friends and view their stories. Irfan: I am not lying. Improve the way you speak first. Talk calmly and I will listen to you. Apsorn: You have created problems for me. If you do not give me the money, I will come to you. I have to pay my room rent and my daughter's bike payments. If you do not return the money, I will have to pay even more. Irfan: The matter concerning KK is from a month or two ago. I did not message her; I only viewed her story. Apsorn: You are lying. If you do not give me anything, I will come. Irfan: Fine, come. Come, then we will see. Apsorn: You have created trouble for me, so I will create trouble for you too. Irfan's WhatsApp chat with the Thai woman's sister Apsorn also handed the police a recording of Irfan's WhatsApp conversation with her sister. In it, her sister is asking for her money back, while Irfan assures her that he will make the payment soon. Apsorn's sister: Am I supposed to keep waiting for my money? Irfan: As far as I can tell, your balance is 2 lakh 66 thousand in Thai currency. I know this is your money. Apsorn's sister: I deposited the money into her account. She will have to return all my money. Irfan: Don't worry, sister. My customer has confirmed the payment. You will receive the money today or tomorrow. Apsorn's sister: When will you give me the money? Irfan: As soon as the payment reaches me, I will give it to you. I understand your problem. I will try to return your money as soon as possible this month. Later, Irfan said that his account had been frozen and that he had been making repeated visits to the police station. Irfan: My wife is in hospital, so please don't message her. My money has been frozen. Give me some time and I will return your money. I have been going to the police station for the past 5-6 days because my money is stuck somewhere. After this, Irfan also sent a photograph of a sub-inspector and a picture of police personnel working on computers. Claimed he would receive ₹10 lakh, used server outage as an excuse In another conversation, Irfan referred to an ₹18 lakh deal. He said he was supposed to receive ₹10 lakh, but the other person was offering only ₹5 lakh. Irfan: I had an ₹18 lakh deal in progress. I was supposed to receive ₹10 lakh, but he was offering only ₹5 lakh. I refused. Otherwise, I would have given you ₹10 lakh today. Just give me a little more time. Apsorn's sister: You could have given ₹5 lakh. You could have paid the remaining amount two or three days later. You have put me in a very difficult situation. Irfan: I am at the bank. An amount has been debited from my account and the money has been frozen. It is stuck on the internal server. Please give me some time; I am getting it fixed. Read what Apsorn alleged in the FIR

stories.title: Missed by 1 mark, was sure of uniform this time:Ran 9 laps, collapsed and died; father weeps over body in Shamli
stories.summary: 23-year-old Vivek Kumar from Shamli suddenly developed chest pain during a PAC recruitment race in Ghaziabad. He stood on the ground for a while, holding a pole and pressing his chest, before collapsing. He was rushed to hospital, but died on the way. The incident took place at 1 p.m. on Tuesday (6 October). On the morning of 7 October, Vivek's body reached Purmafi village, around 20 km from Shamli district headquarters. The eyes of everyone who took part in the funeral procession were filled with tears. His father broke down while clinging to the body. The village elders kept repeating only one thing: Vivek used to say that he had missed selection by one mark last time and that this time he would return only after wearing the uniform. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited Vivek's village in Un tehsil. Read the full report... Father burst into tears before he could speak An eerie silence hung over the village. The elders sat on wooden platforms and charpais, talking only about Vivek. Meanwhile, seeing our team, an elderly man gestured for us to sit in an empty space nearby. In the sombre atmosphere, we somehow gathered the courage to ask about Vivek. Vivek's father, Balendra Singh, burst into tears before he could say anything. The villagers somehow managed to calm him down. A young man sitting nearby offered him water. After taking two sips, he stared silently for a while at the people coming and going along the distant road. Once he had composed himself, he began speaking. "Papa, I will definitely get the marks this time..." Farmer Balendra said, "Vivek was my only son. He would always say, 'I will definitely wear the uniform. Last time, I missed it by just one mark. This time, I will come back wearing khaki.'" The farmer father had nurtured his only son's dreams by toiling in the fields. Every day, his mother prayed that stars would shine on her son's shoulders. Incident at Govindpuri ground in Ghaziabad No one had imagined that the racing track of the 47th Battalion PAC, Govindpuram (Ghaziabad), would become the final ground of Vivek's life on 6 October. The race began, and his legs were moving swiftly towards the finish. But suddenly, his pace faltered and Vivek collapsed unconscious. Coach recognised his talent and secured his admission Vivek's story was not just that of a candidate, but also of a talented sportsperson's struggle. While studying at the village primary school, Vivek's talent blossomed as he played volleyball at a nearby ground. Coach Bharat Veer (Babla) recognised his talent and secured his admission to Veer Bahadur Sports Academy in Gorakhpur. As the family's only son, he became aware of his responsibilities. He left the sport midway and returned to the village. He then began preparing for the police recruitment exam alongside his BA studies. Villagers say that Vivek's father was also a good sportsperson. He played cricket. Coach says - Vivek was the best among 35 players Vivek's coach Bharat Veer says, "Around 35 players play volleyball in the village. Vivek was the best and most hardworking among them. He had to give up the sport because of his family, but he never lost courage. Joining the police became his sole passion. Vivek had also appeared in two other recruitment drives before the one in Ghaziabad. The previous recruitment drive was held in Pilibhit. He missed out by one mark. Friend said: Met him at the station on 4 October; he was very happy Vivek's close friend, Vivek Tomar, said that he had met Vivek at Hind Railway Station on 4 October. He was extremely excited about the recruitment. He kept saying that his preparation was complete this time and that the khaki uniform would be his. When news of Vivek's death reached the village on the night of 6 October, his family could not believe it either. His anxious father repeatedly called his son's number, but there was only ringing on the other end. When Jhinjhana (Shamli) police officially confirmed the news, the house erupted in cries of grief. Funeral held in a sombre atmosphere When Vivek's mortal remains reached Purmafi village on 7 October, the atmosphere became so sombre that even the eyes of those who had come to offer comfort filled with tears. His grieving mother and elder sister Savita were inconsolable. His last rites were performed that afternoon. Thanabhawan MLA Ashraf Ali and former MLA Rao Waris visited Vivek's home, met his family and expressed their grief. The son whom his farmer father had hoped to see in a khaki uniform was left behind forever in the race of life. Now, only stories of Vivek's games and his unfulfilled dream remain in the lanes of Purmafi village.

stories.title: Case filed against woman SI, cop in Varanasi:Victim says they entered home at night, picked up son; showed arrest next day and sent him to jail
stories.summary: A case has been registered against woman Sub-Inspector (SI) Sandhya Jaiswal and an unidentified police officer at Cholapur police station in Varanasi. The action was taken on the court's orders. The woman had alleged that the police officers entered her home on the night of 22 July and took her son away without any offence having been committed. The next day, his arrest was shown and he was sent to jail in a case. The woman has also claimed that she filed a complaint about the matter on the IGRS portal. Based on the application submitted to the court and the evidence presented, the court had directed Cholapur police to register a case. Here is what the case is about Sushila Devi, a resident of Dasnipur in the Cholapur police station area, identified herself as a Scheduled Caste woman in the application submitted to the court. She alleged that at around 3 a.m. on the night of 22 July 2026, her family members were sleeping at home. During this time, Sandhya Jaiswal, the then in-charge of Murdaha outpost, arrived at her house with two constables. It is alleged that the police officers entered the house and began abusing her, taking her son's name. They then woke her son and detained him before taking him to the police station. The woman alleges that she was also treated indecently during the incident and that casteist slurs were used against her. Put on a phone call with lawyer and told to come to the police station to discuss the matter According to Sushila Devi, she called her lawyer and had him speak to the police officers. It is alleged that the police told her during the conversation that a case had been registered against her son and that she should come to the police station to discuss the matter. The woman said that when she reached the police station, she was not immediately given any information about her son. The woman told the court that a case was registered after around 1 p.m., after her son had been taken from the house at night. He was then sent to jail on 23 July. Sushila Devi alleges that her son had committed no crime and that the police first took him from his home and later sent him to jail after showing him as arrested. Allegations linked to case involving photo editing on social media In her application, the woman also mentioned another case. According to her, she had submitted an application in court on 29 January. She alleged that Anjana Kumari, a resident of the Bhelupur police station area, was editing photographs of her and her family members and posting them on social media, thereby defaming her. Based on the complaint, a case was registered on the court's directions. Sushila Devi alleged that her son was falsely implicated in a case to benefit Anjana Kumari in this matter and to put pressure on her. Sushila Devi challenged the police action by filing an application in court. She accused the police of entering her house and taking her son away, showing his arrest later and using casteist slurs, among other allegations. Based on the evidence presented, the court directed Cholapur police to register a case against the police personnel concerned. Police registered the case under these sections Cholapur police station in-charge inspector Sadhuban Ram Gautam said that, on the court's directions, a case had been registered against sub-inspector Sandhya Jaiswal and unidentified police personnel. According to the police, the case was registered under Sections 127(2), 115(2) and 333 of the BNS and Section 3(1)(d) of the SC/ST Act, and further action is under way.

stories.title: Rain amid floods in Lucknow, Palassio Mall turns island:IIIT campus submerged, Gomti reaches disaster management office; alert in 42 cities
stories.summary: The weather has worsened again in Uttar Pradesh amid the floods. Intermittent rain has been lashing five cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Sitapur and Sultanpur, since morning. The Gomti river in Lucknow continues to remain in spate. The water level has been rising for the 10th consecutive day. Plasio Mall has turned into an island, while knee-deep water has accumulated on the roads around it. Water has reached Ekana Stadium and the disaster management office. The IIIT campus is also inundated. As a result, the institute has been closed until further orders and examinations have been postponed. In the Faizullaganj area, around 40,000 homes have been inundated with 5-6 feet of water for the past eight days. A rain alert has been issued for 42 districts today. Atul Singh, a scientist in Lucknow, said a western disturbance has become active over Uttar Pradesh, leading to the change in weather.

stories.title: Kanpur siblings arrested for Rs 45,000 PM housing fraud:Duped several people with fake allotment letters
stories.summary: A brother and sister accused of cheating people on the pretext of securing them houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana have been arrested by Jajmau police in Noida. The accused took money from people by guaranteeing them housing and handed them fake allotment and possession letters. Jajmau residents Asif Mansoori and Amit Gautam had lodged a case against the accused. The investigation revealed that several people had been cheated in the same manner, following which a reward of ₹10,000 each was announced for the two accused. Non-bailable warrants had also been issued against the accused by the court. With the help of the surveillance team, police arrested Satyam Tiwari and his sister Ojस्वी Tiwari in Noida and sent them to jail. ₹45,000 taken by issuing fake allotment letters ACP Ashutosh Singh said the complainants had alleged that Rajesh Tiwari had got forms filled for the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana through his son Satyam Tiwari, daughter Ojasvi Tiwari and associate Naushad Ali. The accused took ₹45,000 from them, guaranteeing that they would be provided housing. They were then handed a fake allotment letter and possession letter for the housing scheme. When they learnt about this some time later, they lodged a complaint with the police. The investigation revealed that the accused had similarly taken money from other people as well, promising to arrange housing for them. ₹10,000 reward announced for each of the two The investigation confirmed the allegations, while the allotment and possession letters provided by the accused were also found to be fake. The police then announced a reward of ₹10,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Satyam Tiwari and Ojasvi Tiwari. The court also issued non-bailable warrants against both of them. With the help of the surveillance team, Jajmau police arrested both men in Noida. After presenting them in court, the police sent them to jail. Police raids are underway to find the other accused named in the case.

stories.title: 4 blackbucks die at Kanpur Zoo in 15 days:Doctor says infection spreads through tabanid flies; deaths also reported in 2015
stories.summary: The deaths of blackbucks at Kanpur Zoo show no sign of stopping. Four blackbucks have died in the past 15 days. Following the deaths, a team of wildlife experts from the Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar-Bareilly, reached Kanpur Zoo on Tuesday. The team inspected the blackbuck enclosure and conducted a post-mortem examination on one of the dead animals. The viscera and other samples have been taken to Bareilly for testing. In its preliminary examination, the team suspected a haemoprotozoan infection, but the actual cause of death will be clear only after the report is received. Infection spreads through fly bites Dr Mohammed Nasir of Kanpur Zoo said the infection can spread from one deer to another through a Tabanid fly. After biting an infected deer, the same fly can transmit the infection to another deer when it bites it. He said that once the infection enters the bloodstream, deer begin showing symptoms such as eating less, reduced movement and weakness. As their condition worsens, they may suddenly collapse while walking and die. Similar symptoms were also seen in Raipur in 2015 According to Dr Nasir, similar symptoms were seen among blackbucks at Nandan Van in Raipur in 2015. The deer also died around October at that time. The disease was correctly identified several months later, in February. Scientists who came to Kanpur Zoo for an investigation also said that the symptoms seen in the deer were similar to those in the incidents reported in Raipur. In view of this, the zoo administration has begun taking precautionary measures. 26 of the 87 deer vaccinated Dr Nasir said that the zoo has a total of 87 blackbucks. In view of the infection, 26 blackbucks were vaccinated on Wednesday. The remaining blackbucks are also being monitored. In addition, the blackbuck enclosure has been cleaned. Lime and medicines have also been sprayed to prevent the infection and flies. Letter sent to IVRI after deaths Dr Nasir said that in recent days, the blackbucks had been suddenly collapsing while walking and dying within a short time. Zoo doctors Nasir and Katiyar were treating the blackbucks, but after the continuous deaths, the zoo administration, considering the seriousness of the matter, decided to have the case investigated by experts from IVRI Bareilly. The zoo director sent a letter to IVRI. Following this, a team of experts reached Kanpur Zoo on Tuesday. The team included senior scientist Dr M. Karikalan, senior scientist Dr Akhilesh Kumar and technician Adarsh Kumar. The team first inspected the blackbuck enclosure. A post-mortem examination was then conducted on one of the dead blackbucks, and its viscera along with other samples were taken to Bareilly for testing. No permanent veterinary officer for one and a half years Kanpur Zoo has not had a permanent veterinary officer for around one and a half years. At present, the wildlife are being cared for by contract doctors. This has raised questions about regular health check-ups, timely treatment, vaccination and the cleanliness of the enclosures. However, the actual cause of the blackbucks' deaths will become clear only after the IVRI investigation report is received.

Gorakhpur’s Anshika wins wrestling gold in Hong Kong:Started in Class 5, now wants to train women wrestlers for India
stories.summary: International wrestler Anshika Yadav, who hails from Gorakhpur, has brought honour to the country at the international level through her hard work and dedication. She won gold after putting in an outstanding performance at the International Championship held in Hong Kong. She has also been honoured by the governor for this achievement. Anshika is the first girl from her village to take up wrestling. Seeing her ability, other girls were inspired as well. They are now undergoing wrestling training and want to represent the country like her. Anshika is currently living in Bengaluru under JSW and pursuing further training. Anshika says that she wants to help girls from villages progress in wrestling so that they can establish their identity and learn self-defence as well. Started wrestling in the fifth grade Anshika, 17, who lives in the small village of Jamouli Bazar in Chauri Chaura, said she was studying at a school in the village. When she was in the fifth grade, a kabaddi competition was organised at her school, in which she took part. During the same event, a small wrestling competition was also held. At that time, Anshika knew nothing about wrestling. Even so, she put in an outstanding performance. The teachers were very pleased to see the way she played. They felt that the girl could progress in this field. Wrestled at the village akhara Then the teachers spoke to Anshika's father. At the time, he was not willing to accept that a girl should take up wrestling. He was then persuaded. One day, he sent her to an akhara located around 3 kilometres from their home. When he saw his daughter's performance himself, he decided to support her further. Anshika practised at the same wrestling arena for a long time. Seeing her growing interest in wrestling, her father enrolled her in a sports college, where she received excellent training in wrestling alongside her studies. Guided by her coach's discipline and driven by her own dedication, Anshika first competed at the local level. Despite limited resources, she continued to progress. Gradually, she made a name for herself by competing at the state level. She then established herself at the national level as well. Anshika also represented India at an international championship held in Hong Kong and brought glory to the country by winning gold. Honoured by the Governor She has also been honoured for this by Governor Anandiben Patel. Anshika has competed at national level eight times and at international level once so far. She is currently living and training in Bengaluru under JSW's sponsorship. Inspired 15 to 20 girls to take up wrestling Anshika said she was the first girl from her village to take up wrestling. Now, inspired by her, 15 to 20 girls have also entered the field and are training in an effort to progress further. Anshika's father, Murlidhar Yadav, works for the Railways. Her mother, Malti Devi, is a homemaker. Anshika is the youngest of four siblings. Her elder sister Preeti is married, while her other sister, Pooja, is engaged to be married. Her brother, Jitendra Yadav, is a CRPF personnel. Anshika Yadav is pursuing a Bachelor of Physical Education and Sports. She will take part in the Senior State Championship on 23 October, which will be held in Gorakhpur.

Carpet with 45 lakh knots, 50 animals hidden in design:Jaipur rug made from saree waste, claimed to last 200 years; buyers from 56 countries at Bhadohi Expo
stories.summary: The 50th India Carpet Expo at Bhadohi’s Carpet Expo Mart brought together some of the most unique examples of Indian handmade carpets. A Kashmiri ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet made with 45 lakh knots and Jaipur carpets made from sari waste were among the biggest attractions at the expo. The expo ended on October 7. More than 400 buyers from 56 countries, including the US and Europe, visited Bhadohi to see Indian carpets. Stalls of 300 exporters and weavers from four states were set up at the expo. Weavers from Andhra Pradesh took part for the first time. ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet gets most attention The ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet made by weavers from Jammu and Kashmir was one of the biggest highlights of the expo. Made from mulberry silk, the carpet stood out for its design and fine work of 45 lakh hand-tied knots. More than 50 animals and birds, including peacocks, parrots, deer and nightingales, have been shown among the branches and leaves of the tree. From a distance, the design looks like a canvas painting, but its fine details become clear when seen up close. The shine of mulberry silk makes the design stand out even more. Kashmiri exporter Mehraj Jan said the price of a carpet depends on the fine work that goes into making it. Three weavers took 14 months to make this carpet, which measures 6x9 feet and weighs around 12 kg. The carpet uses 25 to 30 colours, making it even more special. It is part of the premium carpet range and is priced at ₹9,200 per square foot. Mehraj, who has been taking part in the India Carpet Expo for 16 years, said three generations of his family have been making carpets. He said business was good this time because of the presence of 10 BRICS countries. New buyers were also seen at the stall, with the ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet getting the most attention. Jaipur carpets made from sari waste Carpets at Jaipur-based Omkar Vijay’s stall were also selling quickly. What made them different was the material used to make them. These carpets are made from waste fabric left over during sari production. The material that was once treated as waste is now being sold in the market for around ₹1,000 per kg. The carpets were being presented to foreign buyers as products that can last for at least 200 years. Omkar said making these carpets is a time-consuming process. A sketch is first made on the fabric, after which sari fabric is selected according to the colour and pattern. One carpet can use up to 56 different colours, with different shades mixed to create the design. The weaving takes around four months, followed by another month of finishing. Overall, three workers take around five months to complete one carpet. Around 100 knots are woven into every square foot of the carpet. The designs are based on antique patterns that are 100 to 200 years old. Omkar, whose family has been making carpets for four generations, said around 90% of the carpets at the expo had been sold. The carpets are priced at ₹2,760 per square foot and can last around 200 years. Similar old-style antique carpets have also been used at Jaipur’s City Palace. New buyers from Russia and Türkiye also showed interest. Andhra Pradesh weaver joins expo for first time Imtiaz Ahmed from Andhra Pradesh took part in the expo for the first time. His family has been making carpets for six generations. Imtiaz said around 22 to 25 companies in Andhra Pradesh are involved in the carpet business, with around 100 to 200 people working in the trade. He said expos like this give weavers direct access to foreign buyers. “We do not have to look for new markets ourselves,” he said. Bhadohi’s tiger carpet also attracts buyers A special ‘Tiger Carpet’ at Bhadohi-based Bismillah’s stall also attracted buyers. The 6x9-foot carpet is made of pure silk and takes three to four months to complete. Bismillah said the carpet goes through 25 to 30 steps, from making the design to weaving and finishing. Different workers are involved at different stages. The carpet is priced at around ₹736 per square foot. Buyers from Belgium, France and Germany have already purchased similar carpets. The tiger design is considered a special product in the floor-covering category. US buyers look for neutral shades Aman Anand, who came to the expo from the US, said Indian carpets have good demand in the American market. He said buyers in the US prefer carpets in neutral shades. The size of homes there is also one reason for this preference. Weaver makes PM Modi’s picture on carpet Varanasi-based weaver Gyan Devi has made a carpet featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s picture. She said she had met Modi in Kashi, where he spoke to her with a smile. After that meeting, she thought of making his picture on a carpet. She said the carpet took several months of hard work to complete. Gyan Devi is from Kamalgaon and does hand weaving. She earns around ₹400 a day from weaving. During the inauguration of the expo, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also visited Gyan Devi’s stall and saw her work. He asked her about her earnings. The Carpet Export Promotion Council (CEPC) had invited Gyan Devi to the expo so that foreign buyers and other visitors could see how weavers make carpets by hand. Her husband, Jokhan Bind, works in colour dyeing for carpets. Gyan Devi’s story is not just about one family’s livelihood, but also shows the work of the large number of artisans whose hands have given Indian carpets their identity. Around 10 years ago, Gyan Devi was also honoured by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Gujarat. Carpets worth up to ₹46 crore sold at expo An estimated ₹36.8 crore to ₹46 crore worth of carpets were sold at the 50th India Carpet Expo in Bhadohi. Exporters are hopeful that the presence of foreign buyers will bring more orders in the coming months. More than 212 foreign buyers and 231 buying representatives from 56 countries attended the expo, taking the total number of foreign visitors to more than 400. Artisans who deal with foreign buyers said good weaving alone is not enough for the overseas market. Buyers’ preferences for colours, designs and carpet sizes also have a major impact on business.

stories.title: Akhilesh unwilling to give more than 55-60 seats:Congress builds pressure with smaller parties; how complicated is seat-sharing?
stories.summary: The seat-sharing issue between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections is becoming increasingly complicated. Congress wants to resolve the matter within October itself. For the first time, the party’s working state president and MP Imran Masood has softened his stance and is now demanding “respectable seats”. On the other hand, SP MP from Pratapgarh Shivpal Singh Patel has described Congress’s demand for 150 seats as completely impractical. He argued that the SP has around 125 MLAs in UP, while Congress has only two. Therefore, Congress’s actual standing is limited to 10-20 seats. Even giving it 50 seats would be a very big concession. Congress is trying to put pressure on the SP by bringing smaller parties in UP into its fold. The question is, why have Akhilesh Yadav and Congress’s top leadership, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, not been able to hold talks on seat-sharing? Even after keeping itself away from the leadership change in UP Congress and the MLC elections, why has the party still been unable to secure the seats it wants from the SP? Read the full story… Congress has come down from 200 to 150 seats, now demanding respectable seats Congress had initially demanded 200 seats from the SP for the UP Assembly elections. State in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had even described Congress as the “elder brother”. He had said that there would be no compromise on anything less than an equal share. However, Congress leaders have been gradually softening their stance. The same UP in charge who had demanded 200 seats is now talking about 150. On October 7, working UP Congress president Imran Masood made it clear by talking about a respectable number of seats that Congress has now completely bowed before the SP. By not fielding candidates in the MLC elections, Congress has already sent a message that it is not going against the SP. The question is, how many seats does Congress actually want? Senior journalist Hisam Siddiqui provides the answer. He says Congress wants to re-establish itself in UP. This will only be possible if it has at least one strong face in every district. Therefore, Congress is trying to contest 75-80 seats in the UP Assembly elections. It wants one seat in every district and more than one seat in districts such as Amethi, Rae Bareli and Saharanpur. In other words, the “respectable” number of seats for Congress is being considered to be between 75 and 80. Why is it difficult for the SP to fulfil this demand from Congress? Congress’s organisational base in UP is no secret. In several districts, its organisation is virtually non-existent. Senior journalist Rajendra Prasad says the SP is contesting the 2027 Assembly elections in UP with the aim of forming the government. It also knows that if it misses the opportunity in 2027, it could meet the same fate as Mamata Banerjee, Uddhav Thackeray and the DMK. As of today, the SP is Congress’s strongest ally in the INDIA bloc. The BJP is trying to weaken the alliance further by defeating a strong ally like the SP in UP. This is why the SP is assessing every single seat this time. If the SP gives Congress 75-80 seats as per its demand, only 320-325 seats would remain for the SP to contest. In such a situation, reaching the 202-seat mark would become difficult for the SP. The SP wants Congress to contest with the same level of strength so that reaching the majority mark becomes easier. This is why SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had earlier said that there is only one formula for seat-sharing: victory. Congress should tell the SP which candidates it plans to field on which seats. The SP wants Congress to at least provide it with a list of 50 such seats. Sources associated with the SP say that Congress had been asked for this list, but it has not provided it yet. This is why the seat-sharing issue between the two parties has not been resolved. Rahul-Priyanka and Akhilesh have not yet spoken about seat-sharing Sources associated with the SP and Congress claim that the top leadership of both parties has understood one thing: the UP Assembly elections and the 2029 Lok Sabha elections will be contested together as an alliance. In other words, the SP-Congress alliance is likely to continue for a long time. The alliance will benefit in 2029 only if it manages to win UP in 2027. According to senior journalist Hisam Siddiqui, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi have not yet held talks on seat-sharing. He also claims that the seat-sharing formula in UP will be decided only with the consent of these three leaders. Apart from them, whatever other leaders are saying has no significance. So, is Congress trying to bring smaller parties on board to prepare its list? In recent days, several leaders of smaller parties active in UP have met Rahul and Priyanka. Apart from this, Congress has continued to bring several prominent faces into the party. Former minister Swami Prasad Maurya, who was active in UP politics under the banner of his own party, has also met Rahul and Priyanka along with his son Utkrisht Maurya. It is being said that the father-son duo will contest the UP elections on the Congress symbol. Similarly, Ghazipur’s Dr Sanjay Chauhan, who runs a party representing the Chauhan community, and Pankaj Niranjan of Apna Dal (Kamerawadi) have also met Rahul Gandhi. Pankaj Niranjan is the husband of MLA Pallavi Patel. It is believed that all these leaders will contest the Assembly elections on the Congress symbol. Earlier, Hemant Chaudhary had merged his Jan Sardar Party with Congress. Hemant Chaudhary had previously been active in politics with Apna Dal (S). His party had a significant influence among the Kurmi community. Hemant Chaudhary is considered to have influence over around 8-10 seats in Basti and Siddharthnagar districts. Eight-time former MLA Pandit Shyam Sundar Sharma, a prominent figure in Mathura politics, has also joined Congress. Congress wants to prepare its list with the help of these leaders from smaller parties so that it can demonstrate the weight of its demand when negotiating seat-sharing with the SP. SP may adopt the 2022 Assembly election formula Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says both parties will have to show flexibility in the alliance. The SP will have to give Congress more than 70 seats under any circumstances. The SP may also adopt the formula used in the 2022 Assembly elections, under which the candidates would belong to the SP, but the Congress symbol would be used. This means that if Congress does not have strong candidates, the SP could offer an alternative as part of the seat-sharing arrangement. In 2022, the SP had fielded its own candidates on several seats allotted to the SBSP. Pallavi Patel herself won the election on the SP symbol and entered the Assembly.

stories.title: ‘Hang daughter-in-law and her lover’:Meerut mother says, ‘They had my son bitten by snake; let her die as he suffered, only then will I find peace’
stories.summary: Amit Kashyap’s mother Munesh Devi came and sat outside the ADJ 12 court in Meerut on Wednesday, expecting the verdict in her son’s murder case and demanding that his daughter-in-law Ravita and her lover be hanged. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Munesh said, “After the brutal way my son was murdered and made to be bitten by a snake, I want the murderous daughter-in-law and her lover to be hanged. Just as she made my son suffer, I want them to die in agony too. Only then will my soul find peace.” She said Ravita not only destroyed her own marriage with the help of her lover but also left three children orphaned, adding that she was now living only with the hope that her son’s killers would receive such a punishment that she would feel justice had been done. She hoped that the court would announce a severe punishment today. However, the court found Ravita and her lover Amardeep guilty of murder. October 16 has been fixed as the date for sentencing. The murder took place on April 17, 2025. The court delivered its verdict after recording the statements of more than 12 witnesses over 16 hearings. Read in detail what happened in court and the complete story of the case… Mother says, ‘If they are not sentenced to death, I will approach the High Court’ Mother Munesh Devi said, “My son Amit was the father of three children. Since he has been gone, his laughter and voice make me cry every moment. His three innocent children still ask, ‘Where is our father? Where is our mother?’ His father could not bear the shock of his son’s murder either and died after suffering emotionally. Now I want my son’s killers to be sentenced to death. If they are not hanged, I will also appeal in the High Court. I will ensure justice for my innocent grandchildren and myself.” Brother says, ‘If Ravita did not want to live with Amit, she could have left him. Why did she murder him?’ Amit’s brother Sandeep said, “If Ravita did not want to live with Amit, she could have told him. She could have left him. But she brutally murdered my brother. His post-mortem also confirmed that Amit died due to strangulation. After this, we came here hoping that the court would pronounce its verdict today. We hope the court will ensure justice for us. We want nothing less than the death penalty. I will continue to demand justice and seek the death penalty for my brother’s killers.” Government lawyer says, 'Ravita and Amardeep guilty of murder and destroying evidence' Farzana, the government lawyer who represented Amit’s side, said, “The court has found Amardeep and Ravita guilty. October 16 has been fixed for sentencing. Twelve witnesses were presented by our side in this case. Among them were the complainant Monu Kashyap and Munesh, who was also an eyewitness. On the night of the murder, she saw him coming to and leaving her son’s room. Ravita was in an illicit relationship with Amardeep. Amardeep used to visit Ravita’s house. “There were several fights as well. Later, the two conspired to eliminate Amit Kashyap, after which Ravita became involved in religious rituals. A few days later, Ravita planned that she needed a snake for the worship. The snake charmer then provided a rat snake. Amit was subsequently strangled to death. “Ravita and her lover Amardeep have been found guilty of murder and destroying evidence. On the night of the murder, the locations of Ravita and Amardeep were also found at the house.” Lawyer says, 'Both were located at the house on the night of the murder' The lawyer representing Amit said, “The phone locations of Ravita and Amardeep were found at the scene of the crime. Both were seen coming to and leaving the place. Their illicit relationship was several days old. They had also been warned about it, and the deceased Amit’s mother had seen them coming and going. On this basis, both were found guilty.” Read the complete story of the husband’s murder and the snake-bite plot Wife had said, 'He used to do things with me that were even worse than rape' While being taken to jail, the accused wife, Ravita, had said, “He (the husband, Amit) used to beat me every day. He used to do things with me that were even worse than rape. He would say, ‘I will turn you into a prostitute and make you work in the sex trade.’ He knew that I spoke to Amardeep on the phone. My husband himself made me speak to Amardeep on the phone. Then he told me that he would call Amardeep to our house. He said I would have to help him kill Amardeep. Then he would kill me too.” Lover had said, 'Amit sent men after me to kill me, so I killed him' Before being sent to jail, Ravita’s accused lover Amardeep had said, “A few days ago, I had an argument with Amit over a transaction of ₹3,500. Some people then got us to settle the matter. Even after that, Amit sent some men after me to kill me. “When I came to know about this, I plotted Amit’s murder to save my own life. Amardeep said there is a village called Mohammadpur in the Mawana area, where many snake charmers live. I bought the snake from them for ₹1,000. One of the snake charmers’ associates came here and sold me the snake.”

stories.title: BJP Rajya Sabha candidate says Samajwadi ‘more infamous than Munni’:Says uncle shown in name of backward class, wealthy man given ticket; asks, 'Where is Akhilesh’s PDA?'
stories.summary: “Rajya Sabha candidates have just been announced. Where was PDA visible there? The SP gave a ticket to a wealthy industrialist. In the name of the backward class, his uncle was brought in, while there was no one from the Dalit community. They stopped at two. Had there been a third candidate, perhaps they would have brought in a criminal…” This was said by BJP Rajya Sabha candidate and state president of the BJP OBC Morcha, Prakash Pal. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, he said that even after being in power four times in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party has become discredited among every section of society. “Today, the SP is more infamous than ‘Munni’. Now even uncle Shivpal has to seek permission to enter the party office.” On Akhilesh calling former Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai ‘Chirkut’, Prakash Pal said, “This shows how Akhilesh views his own alliance partners.” He said that the importance of the uncle and the family has now ended in the SP. He also attacked the SP chief over giving preference to an industrialist for a Rajya Sabha ticket and taking jibes at leaders of alliance partners. Read the full interview… Question: The SP is trying to woo OBCs and Dalits through the ‘PDA Yatra’. How will you counter it? Answer: We do not need to counter it. The SP has been in power four times. Even after that, it has become a discredited party among all sections of society. Earlier, some people said PDA meant ‘Power Family Development Authority’. But now even the uncle is not being given any importance. We are getting reports that Shivpal and Dharmendra are also not allowed to enter the party office without Akhilesh’s permission. When the uncle himself is not being given any importance in the party, the new meaning of PDA will now be ‘Power of Dimple Akhilesh’. The uncle is not there, and neither is the family. Question: Why did Akhilesh Yadav not field a third candidate? Answer: We feel that he himself got shocked by the prospect of a possible defeat and escaped by putting out a tweet. He said that the fight is not for three seats but for all 403 seats. I would say that if someone does not have the courage to contest three seats, how will they contest all 403? Question: Akhilesh called Ajay Rai ‘Chirkut’. How do you see this? Answer: This raises a very big question about the status with which he views his alliance partners and their presidents, that he calls them ‘Chirkut’. When he considers the state president of a party that is bigger than his own party, has more MPs, and whose family has produced Prime Ministers of India for several generations, to be a ‘Chirkut’, you can understand how he must view his other people. Question: The SP and BSP are demanding a caste census. Why is it not being conducted? Answer: Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav kept saying that we would conduct a caste census at all costs. But the day PM Modi announced it, no one is coming forward to take credit for it. The reason is that the Prime Minister has announced a caste census for Muslims along with a caste census of Hindus. Now, if these people come forward to take credit for it, Muslims will chase them away. Let me tell you that there are 33 Waqf Boards in the country. Not a single Pasmanda, who belongs to the backward class, is a chairman or member anywhere. This is the truth of their politics. Question: The state presidents of the SP and BSP are from the Pal community. Is this a challenge for the BJP? Answer: It is not just about reaching out to the Pal community. This community is firmly standing with the BJP. The BJP has given respect to the backward classes. Prime Minister Modi has consistently worked in the interests of the backward classes. Our effort is to ensure that government schemes reach every section of society and that people benefit from them.

stories.title: Owaisi says Muslims belong to no one:Claims BJP-Akhilesh have a ‘fixed match’; one demolishes mosques, madrasas, the other takes Muslim votes
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi strongly criticised the Samajwadi Party and the parties part of the INDI alliance in Shravasti on Sunday evening. He said, "Muslims in Uttar Pradesh or the country are not any political party's fiefdom. Muslims are not your hereditary property. We are human beings, not just voters. If you consider us your hereditary property, you will find out what that means in the upcoming Assembly elections." Owaisi alleged that the Samajwadi Party took votes from Muslims but built its palaces of power by shattering their dreams. He told Muslims, "There is no need to be afraid or panic. The BJP must certainly be stopped. The BJP should not form the government here for a third time." Now, read about Owaisi's 4 major points... 37 graveyards and shrines demolished: A large number of madrasas were shut down in Uttar Pradesh, and bulldozers were used to demolish more than 18 madrasas. Around 37 graveyards and shrines were also demolished. Why did Samajwadi Party workers not reach the spot during this period? SP workers did not come because they know that these are symbols of poor Muslims. This system of injustice must now be ended. Why so much hatred for mosques and madrasas: Why does CM Yogi hate mosques, madrasas and graveyards so much? Madrasas impart knowledge and teach people to become better human beings. Discipline is taught at shrines and khanqahs, but the Chief Minister has a problem with these institutions. Match fixed between BJP and SP: Owaisi said that a "fixed match" was being played between Yogi and Akhilesh. According to him, Yogi demolishes madrasas and religious sites on one side, while Akhilesh works to consolidate Muslim votes on the other. Now, Asaduddin Owaisi, a man of principles, has emerged between the two. Owaisi planted his flag: I want to tell the people and leaders of the Samajwadi Party and these so-called secular parties, remember, you keep saying that if Owaisi enters the fray, the votes will be divided. Listen, Samajwadi people, this is not your feast, and we are not guests at your feast. This is not your feast, and we are not guests at your feast. This politics is a fair of Indian democracy, and in this Indian politics, Owaisi has come and planted his flag, and this flag will continue to fly. Rally had been postponed on 27 September due to bad weather This AIMIM public meeting was originally scheduled for 27 September but was cancelled due to bad weather. Owaisi held the meeting at Bhinga market at 5 p.m. on Sunday. Haji Daddan Khan, who was expelled from the BSP, is a potential candidate for the Bhinga Assembly seat. Daddan Khan was the BSP candidate from the Shravasti seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. After joining the AIMIM, Daddan Khan held a roadshow in September. Police registered a case against AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali, Daddan Khan and several others on charges of holding the roadshow without permission. Owaisi on alliance: We have conveyed our position to Akhilesh Asaduddin Owaisi said in Lucknow on Sunday, "We say that we will not roll out the carpet; we are not a vote bank. We should get our rightful share. Obviously, those who do not accept this truth must be feeling troubled." In an alliance with the Samajwadi Party, Owaisi said, "Our party has made its position clear. We have also cited the example of Bihar. Whatever alliance is formed will be announced to you." AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali made a major statement. He said that if an alliance is formed without Muslim leadership and without AIMIM being part of it, it would not be an alliance but a deception. Such an alliance would exploit society's oppressed, Muslim, deprived and exploited sections.

stories.title: Police bring Atiq Ahmed's shooter Arman to Uttar Pradesh:Parents fear an encounter; spent 3 years in Gaya jail
stories.summary: UP Police are bringing Armaan, an accused in the Umesh Pal murder case in Prayagraj, from Gaya jail. At around 6 p.m. on Sunday, the police received a copy of the transit remand order. Armaan was then taken into custody. He was brought out of Gaya Central Jail in the presence of Bihar Police. The police had him medically examined. He was then taken by road to Prayagraj. Teams from the UP and Bihar police are accompanying him. Armaan will be produced before the Prayagraj district court on Monday. The police will involve him in the investigation into the Umesh Pal murder case. UP Police had been searching for Armaan since the Umesh Pal murder case. It later emerged that he was lodged in Gaya jail in another case. The UP Police then began the process of obtaining transit remand to bring him to Prayagraj. Armaan was a shooter for mafia don Atiq Ahmed. Two pictures of shooter Armaan... Family says, Police did not inform us After learning that Armaan was being taken to Uttar Pradesh, his father, Shameem, and mother, Asgari Khatoon, began fearing a police encounter. They said their son could be killed in an encounter as soon as he was taken to Uttar Pradesh. Arman's father had filed an application in the Gaya court, seeking that Arman not be handed over to the Uttar Pradesh Police. He said that if the police needed to question him, it should be done via video conference. Mother says he is being made a scapegoat Accused Arman's father, Shamim, said, "Most of the accused in the Umesh Pal murder case have already been killed in police encounters. Arman could also be killed in an encounter in the name of recovering a weapon." Arman's mother, Asgari Khatun, said, "My son is being made a scapegoat. Our family is very poor. We do not even have a permanent house of our own to live in." She said Arman had previously lived in Prayagraj, where he did odd jobs. He is not a professional criminal or a major shooter. He has been in jail for the past three years. She appealed to Chief Minister Yogi and the administration to ensure Arman's safety. Arman's younger brother, Imran, said, "We had already expressed fears that my brother's life was in danger. The Uttar Pradesh Police have now taken him to Prayagraj. We fear that something untoward may happen to Arman too. The family will accept whatever verdict the court delivers. But Arman must not be harmed in any way." Armaan's lawyer says jail administration and police colluded Armaan's parents' application was heard on 1 October in the court of Gaya magistrate Saurabh Kumar. The court had rejected the application filed by Armaan's family and lawyer. Armaan's lawyer, Lalit Kumar Gupta, confirmed this. The lawyer accused the police and jail administration. He said, "Armaan's life is in danger. He could be killed in Uttar Pradesh. A conspiracy is being hatched to kill Mohammad Armaan in collusion with the Uttar Pradesh Police and the Gayaji Central Jail administration." We had sought a court appearance via video conference, citing security concerns, but the court rejected the request. Armaan has been lodged in Gaya jail since 27 February 2023. He is being deliberately framed in a case in Uttar Pradesh. Now know how the Uttar Pradesh Police reached Gayaji Jail The Uttar Pradesh Police had been searching for Armaan for the past three years. During this period, it learnt that he was lodged in Gayaji Central Jail. After receiving the information, police from Prayagraj's Dhoomanganj police station reached Gayaji Jail on 30 September. There, the police took Armaan's latest photograph and obtained his thumb impressions on plain paper. After completing the paperwork, the police returned to Prayagraj. It then filed an application for transit remand in the Gaya court on 1 October. Armaan was seen firing alongside Guddu Muslim Umesh Pal and his two government gunners were shot dead in broad daylight in Prayagraj on 24 February 2023. CCTV footage of the incident also emerged. A motorbike rider was seen in the footage. According to the police, Armaan was riding the motorbike, while Guddu Muslim was seated behind him. Armaan had brought Guddu Muslim to the scene on the motorbike. As soon as the motorbike stopped, Guddu Muslim began firing. Armaan also opened fire. After the crime, the two fled the scene on the motorbike.

stories.title: Bhojpuri star Pawan Singh’s mother hospitalised:Emotional hug, wrote ‘Mai hamar duniya’; wife Jyoti also seeks prayers
stories.summary: Bhojpuri star Pawan Singh’s mother, Pratima Devi, has fallen ill. She has been admitted to a hospital in Lucknow. Pawan Singh shared an emotional picture on Instagram. His mother can be seen lying on a hospital bed, while Pawan Singh is seen hugging her. Along with the picture, Pawan Singh wrote, “Maai hamar duniya” (My mother is my world). After the post surfaced, his fans have been praying for his mother’s speedy recovery. Pawan’s close friend Priyanshu Singh also shared a picture of Pratima Devi from the hospital. He said that Pawan Singh’s mother is unwell and appealed to people to pray for her speedy recovery and long life. Wife Jyoti shared VIDEO, wished her a long life Pawan Singh’s wife, Jyoti Singh, also shared pictures and a video of her mother-in-law, Pratima Devi, on social media. She wished her a speedy recovery and prayed to God to bless Pratima Devi with good health and a long life. Pawan is very close to his mother Pawan Singh is known to be very close to his mother. He has spoken about his affection for her on several occasions. Recently, he was also seen massaging his mother’s feet in the promo of his reality show ‘Bhojpuri Bawal’. After news of his mother’s ill health emerged, his fans have been continuously wishing for her speedy recovery. Power Star Pawan Singh released a new song titled ‘Maai’ on Saturday. Pawan Singh himself has sung the song. The lyrics have been written by Prince Priyadarshi, while Priyanshu Singh is its music director.

stories.title: ‘If anyone raises a hand, cut it off’:Minister Sanjay Nishad says, ‘We have given the order, we will get you bail’
stories.summary: A Nishad Party public meeting was held in Sultanpur on Sunday. Cabinet minister and Nishad Party president Dr Sanjay Nishad also arrived at around 4 p.m. He told workers at the meeting, "If anyone raises a hand against you, then after today, the order from us is... break or cut off his hand and throw it away. We will get you bail." Dr Sanjay Nishad also appealed to supporters to hoist the Nishad Party flag at every home. He said, "This flag is a guarantee of the children's future, education, respect and security. If a leader of another party comes to your neighbourhood carrying a flag, chase him away instead of welcoming him." Said-Do not press the button bearing another party's election symbol A public meeting of the Nishad Party was held near Patna Chauraha in Kurebhar. Targeting the Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party, Sanjay Nishad raised the issues of jobs and political representation. He said pressing the button bearing another party's election symbol meant that others benefited from the jobs. He appealed to workers to raise the 'Jai Nishad Raj' flag and strengthen the organisation. Jail is the place for people with a feudal mindset Dr Sanjay Nishad recently referred to a video showing a member of the Nishad community being assaulted and abused in Gorakhpur. He said that people with a feudal mindset were subjecting members of society to atrocities. "I will always stand at the forefront to defend the honour and dignity of the community. Jail is the only place for such people." Referring to the Faizabad incident, he said strict action had been taken after he raised in the Legislative Assembly the case involving atrocities against a daughter of the Nishad community. He also referred to the bulldozer action. We must fight an all-out battle for reservation Sanjay Nishad also raised the issue of reservation by seeking the inclusion of the fishing community in the SC category. He told workers to continue the struggle and remain prepared for an all-out battle to secure the implementation of reservation. He stressed the need to ensure education for children, employment and access to the benefits of government schemes. In view of the upcoming Assembly election, he urged workers to remain active in every village and strengthen the organisation down to the booth level. Workers arrived at the programme from several districts, including Amethi, Ambedkar Nagar, Azamgarh, Mau, Ayodhya and Pratapgarh, besides Sultanpur. A large crowd gathered at the venue. Women also participated. When Dr Sanjay Nishad arrived, the workers raised slogans of "Jai Nishad Raj".

stories.title: 5 feet of water in 40,000 Lucknow homes:Cars submerged, food supplies soaked; patients carried out on cots
stories.summary: The flood situation has become serious in Lucknow. Water levels in the Gomti River have been rising rapidly for the sixth consecutive day. The Faizullaganj area is the worst affected. Water, four to five feet deep, has accumulated in 40,000 homes. Three lakh people have been affected. More than 2,000 people are leaving their homes every day for other neighbourhoods or relatives' houses. Water has reached Hanumant Dham and Lete Hanuman, located along the Gomti Riverfront, as well as Chandrika Devi Temple in Bakshi ka Talab. The administration has temporarily closed the Food Valley near the Gomti Riverfront and Marine Drive. Boats have been deployed to help people. Residents say government boat operators are charging each person ₹100 to ₹150. A boatman said, "We were assigned work here three days ago. We were paid ₹1,000 that day. The administration promised to pay us ₹3,000 a day but is not giving us anything." The threat from snakes and other venomous creatures has also increased. Several diseases are spreading because of the filth. It is claimed that teams have been deployed for relief and healthcare services. Mobile medical units are distributing medicines, chlorine tablets and ORS. However, patients are having to be carried on cots. See the flood pictures-

stories.title: Annu Awasthi to contest from Sisamau:Holds ‘Dev Yatra’ in Kanpur with 50-vehicle convoy; says, ‘I will win by making people laugh’
stories.summary: Kanpur comedian Annu Awasthi announced that he would contest the election from the Sisamau seat. He said, "We will laugh our way to victory there and make the public laugh." In this connection, Annu Awasthi organised a Mitra Milan and Dev Yatra on Sunday. A convoy of more than 50 vehicles took part in the nearly 16-kilometre journey. MP Ramesh Awasthi and film actress Deepti Joshi were also present with Annu. Annu Awasthi said he was making a new beginning with the visit to the deity. "I have an old association with Sisamau," he said. It may be noted that Nasim Solanki is the MLA from Sisamau. The Samajwadi Party may field Nasim again in the next election. See 2 pictures... Annu Awasthi and Deepti Joshi rode in an open jeep Annu Awasthi began the Dev Yatra from the Curfew Car Market in Lajpat Nagar at around 3 p.m. on Sunday. Before the procession began, Annu's daughter Vanshika applied a tilak to him. BJP workers then carried him on their shoulders to the open jeep. During the procession, slogans of "Long live MP Ramesh Awasthi" and "Long live Annu Awasthi" were raised. Annu Awasthi boarded the open jeep. MP Ramesh Awasthi and television actress Deepti Joshi also boarded the jeep with him. Accompanied by a convoy of around 50 vehicles, the procession reached Deputy Padav via Gumti, Darshan Purwa and Deva Nagar. After offering prayers at the Chandrika Devi Temple there, the procession reached the Vankhandeshwar Temple in Sisamau Market. Annu Awasthi performed prayers at the temple. The procession then left for Chunniganj. During the approximately 16-kilometre journey, people carried saffron and tricolour flags. Golden Baba, also known as Manojanand Maharaj, also took part in the procession. Supporters and local people welcomed Annu Awasthi along the route. During the yatra, Annu Awasthi said, “We are making a new beginning with darshan at the temples. I was born in this area and have had a long association with the Vankhandeshwar Temple. People from this area used to win elections while making others cry. Now, their path has become difficult. We will win here by making people laugh and keep the public happy.” Awasthi said, “The people of the constituency have given me immense love, respect and honour. They have now become God for me. From today, I have become a devotee of the people of Sisamau. I will continue to work for them as long as I live.” MP Ramesh Awasthi said, “Our brother Annu Awasthi, a film actor who lives in the hearts of people in Kanpur, took out the Dev Darshan Yatra. I was also invited, which is why I came here.” Irfan Solanki’s family has held Sisamau seat for years Annu Awasthi has announced that he will contest from Kanpur’s Sisamau seat, which has long been held by Irfan Solanki’s family. His wife, Naseem Solanki, is currently the MLA from the constituency. Sisamau has a sizeable Muslim electorate. During the 1991 Ram wave, BJP’s Rakesh Sonkar became the MLA from the seat for the first time. He also won in 1993 and 1996. In 2002, however, Congress wrested the seat from the BJP and retained it in 2007. After the delimitation in 2012, the seat went to the Samajwadi Party, with Irfan Solanki, then an MLA from Arya Nagar, winning from Sisamau. Irfan won the seat again in 2017 and 2022. However, his membership was cancelled after he was convicted in the Jajmau arson case. In the subsequent bypoll, his wife Naseem Solanki defeated BJP’s Suresh Awasthi.

stories.title: Yogi renames Bhadohi district:Says it will now be known as Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi; 5th name change in 32 years
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday announced that Bhadohi district will now be known as ‘Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi’. Speaking at the 50th India Carpet Expo, he said the district would henceforth be known by the new name. Earlier, on July 29, 2026, Yogi had announced in Varanasi that Bhadohi would be renamed ‘Sant Ravidas Nagar’. This is the fifth time Bhadohi’s name has been changed in 32 years. Referring to Sant Ravidas’ message from around 600 years ago, Yogi said he had envisioned a kingdom where everyone had enough food and people lived together without discrimination. He said that today, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, more than 800 million people in the country are receiving free ration. 12 districts in UP whose names were changed Now, know Yogi’s 9 key announcements… 1- University to be formally inaugurated The Chief Minister said Kashi Naresh Government Degree College has received university status. The process of affiliating colleges in the district with the university has also been completed. The university will soon be formally inaugurated and the foundation stone for a new building will be laid. 2- Sant Ravidas Nagar to be connected to Vindhya Expressway Under the expansion of the Ganga Expressway, directions have been issued to connect Sant Ravidas Nagar with the Vindhya Expressway. The DPR for the Madhosingh railway flyover is ready, and the tender process will begin soon. The Chief Minister said development should be carried out by taking everyone along. 3- ODOP gives carpets access to bigger markets The Chief Minister said the ODOP scheme has provided Bhadohi’s carpets with technology, better designs and access to larger markets. Now, 90% of the carpets made here are exported to countries including the US, Germany, Australia, Canada and the UK. 4- Silk cluster accounts for ₹6,100 crore in exports The silk clusters of Sant Ravidas Nagar, Mirzapur and Varanasi account for 60% of the country’s total carpet exports. Sant Ravidas Nagar alone has more than 2,500 MSME units, providing employment to over 5 lakh people. 5- Noida International Airport to be six hours away The Chief Minister said improved connectivity would benefit the carpet industry. After the expansion of the Vindhya Expressway, Noida International Airport will be around six hours away from Sant Ravidas Nagar. 6- No mafia can threaten traders now The Chief Minister said there is no longer an atmosphere of riots, curfews and mafia activity in the state. Traders and entrepreneurs are doing business in a secure environment. 7- Factories rise from 14,000 to over 35,000 He said Uttar Pradesh had around 14,000 factories before 2017, but the number has now crossed 35,000. The state has 96 lakh MSME units. 8- Bhadohi carpet laid in new Parliament building The Chief Minister said the carpet laid in the new Parliament building was also made in Sant Ravidas Nagar. The district has received facilities such as a GI tag, the ODOP platform and the Carpet Expo Mart. 9- International Trade Show showcased UP’s strength to the world According to the Chief Minister, more than 6 lakh people attended the UP International Trade Show held in Greater Noida. Over 2,400 exhibitors and more than 650 foreign buyers participated. Gifts of 112 projects worth ₹1,340 crore The Chief Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 112 projects worth over ₹1,340 crore across the Bhadohi, Aurai and Gyanpur Assembly constituencies. These include 65 inaugurated projects and 47 projects whose foundation stones were laid. The Chief Minister distributed cheques, house keys, appointment letters and Ayushman cards to beneficiaries of various schemes. ₹2 crore was given to Vineet Rai, ₹5 lakh to Pawan Kumar, ₹10 lakh to Gaurav Singh and ₹4.46 crore to Kajal Gautam. Jaydev was handed a house key, Neha and Prinsi received appointment letters as Anganwadi workers, and Jamanadevi was given an Ayushman card. The Chief Minister also inspected stalls set up by various departments. He conducted the annaprashan ceremony for children, performed the god bharai ceremony for pregnant women, and viewed models made by children at a science exhibition. Expo expects ₹500 crore in business Exporters from across the country have set up stalls showcasing their products at the 50th India Carpet Expo. According to the organisers, buyers from 65 countries are expected to attend, with business worth over ₹500 crore likely to be generated. The expo will be held from October 4 to 7.

stories.title: UP Rajya Sabha polls:BJP sends 24 names to Delhi for 8 seats, 2 Brahmin leaders likely
stories.summary: Polling for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh is scheduled for 16 October. The BJP's state unit has sent the central leadership the names of 24 potential candidates for eight seats. Kripa Shankar Singh, who hails from Jaunpur, is also emerging as a contender. Kripa Shankar Singh served as Maharashtra's Minister of State for Home between 2009 and 2024. The BJP fielded him from the Jaunpur seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, although he suffered defeat there. Despite the loss, he has remained active in Jaunpur and the surrounding Purvanchal region. He is considered to have a strong support base among the North Indian community, particularly people from Uttar Pradesh living in Mumbai and Maharashtra. The BP may consider sending him to the Rajya Sabha as part of a strategy to balance the regional and caste equations in Purvanchal. BJP focuses on Brahmin community, 7 prominent names in race for 2 seats According to the panel, Brahmin candidates are almost certain to be given an opportunity for 2 of the 8 Rajya Sabha seats. The party's objective behind this is to reach out to the educated section and send a political message. The prominent names from the Brahmin quota that have been sent to the central leadership include: The contest between these veterans is neck and neck, and the final decision will be taken at the BJP Central Election Committee meeting in Delhi. Jayant Chaudhary preparing to respond to the SP The BJP may give one Rajya Sabha seat to its NDA ally, the RLD. However, an interesting situation has emerged regarding RLD president and Union minister Jayant Chaudhary. Jayant Chaudhary was elected to the Rajya Sabha with the SP's support. A few days ago, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav took a swipe at Jayant, saying, "Those whom I had turned from half-rupees and quarter-rupees into rupees have now left me and gone." Strategists in the RLD and BJP fear that Akhilesh Yadav and the SP could once again exploit the issue in the upcoming Assembly election by alleging that Jayant is in the Rajya Sabha only because of the SP's support. Jayant's supporters want him to resign from his current term and win a fresh Rajya Sabha election with the BJP's support, thereby countering the Opposition's allegations. There is also intense speculation that Jayant's wife, Charu Chaudhary, could be sent to the Rajya Sabha in his place, although no official party source has formally confirmed this so far.

stories.title: Akhilesh dissolves Gorakhpur SP team over slap incident:District president and all leaders removed; clash broke out over seating at press conference
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav has taken major action following the clash at the party’s press conference in Gorakhpur. He has dissolved the district and metropolitan units of the party, along with the executive committees of its frontal organisations. The district president, metropolitan president and all office-bearers and members have been removed. The incident took place on Saturday (October 3) during an SP press conference at the Gorakhpur Journalists’ Press Club. An argument broke out over seating arrangements and later escalated into verbal abuse and a physical altercation. During the clash, Kamlesh Singh, son of SP leader Anshuman Singh, slapped former district president Nagina Sahni. Anshuman Singh was expelled from the party shortly after the incident. He was an aspirant for the SP ticket from the Gorakhpur Rural Assembly seat. A video of the incident also surfaced, further escalating the matter. Meanwhile, on Saturday night, Nagina Sahni filed an FIR at Cantt police station against Anshuman Singh, his two sons Kamlesh and Vimlesh Singh, and 10–12 unidentified people. See two pictures related to the dispute... Conference was being held as part of 'Save Democracy Week' SP district president Brijesh Gautam was holding a press conference about the programme being conducted on the instructions of Akhilesh Yadav. Information was being given about 'Save Democracy Week', which will run from 2 to 8 October. At that point, Anshuman Singh, who is preparing to contest from the rural seat, arrived at the press conference with his supporters. Speaking to the media, Anshuman said, "Most of the chairs in the auditorium were occupied. There was some vacant space in the middle. I had a chair brought and asked Nagina Sahani to move slightly to the side so I could sit. Nagina Sahani refused to move. An argument and scuffle then broke out between the two sides." Anshuman said, ‘A conspiracy to tarnish his image’ Making the allegation, Anshuman Singh said the entire drama was staged to tarnise his image. Former Samajwadi Party district president Nagina Sahani wants to damage his image. Nagina Sahani is also seeking the party ticket from the same Assembly seat that he is seeking to contest in the 2027 election. Nagina Sahani wants his image to be tarnished by creating such a controversy. That is why he is trying to give the incident a political colour. Anshuman accused Nagina Sahani of using abusive language and speaking against the party's candidates. He said, "I did not use any abusive language." Former district president says, ‘I was targeted because they considered me a fisherman’ Nageena Sahani said, "During the press conference, the people accompanying Anshuman Singh began forcibly asking me to vacate my chair. When they were asked to sit in the vacant space, they became intent on fighting. They abused and assaulted me." Accusing Anshuman Singh, Nageena Sahani said, "I belong to the fisherman-Nishad community. For this reason, I was considered weak and targeted. Some people want to establish their dominance through muscle power." Former district president Nagina Sahani lodged a complaint at Cantt police station. A case has been registered against Anshuman Singh, his two sons Kamlesh Singh and Vimlesh Singh, and 10 to 12 unidentified people. 'I have been seeking a ticket for 14 years, but still have not got one' On his claim to contest from the Gorakhpur Rural Assembly seat, Nagina Sahani said, "National president Akhilesh Yadav will decide who gets the ticket. I have been seeking a ticket since 2012, but I have not got one yet." "Those given the ticket by the party work for that candidate. Everyone has the right to seek a ticket, but no one has the right to engage in violence or indiscipline. Some people accompanying Anshuman Singh came to the Press Club carrying illegal weapons." "Journalists from the local and national media were present at the Press Club, so bringing weapons to such a place is a serious matter. I was threatened with death." Asked whether he would lodge a police complaint, Nagina said, "I will decide after discussing the matter with party leaders." Kajal Nishad says: Incident highly condemnable SP leader Kajal Nishad said that 'Save Democracy Week' was being observed over the issue of votes being deleted in the name of SIR. A decision to run the campaign from 2 to 8 October was taken at the INDIA bloc meeting in New Delhi on 30 September. Kajal Nishad said, "Nagina Sahani had said that a woman was sitting next to her and that there was no space there. Following this, abuses were exchanged and a scuffle broke out. This incident is highly condemnable. Every leader has the right to seek a ticket during elections. But there should be no dispute among them like this." SP district president says, ‘Will inform Akhilesh ji’ SP district president Brijesh Gautam said that Anshuman Singh had arrived with some members of his family during the press conference. He said he was presenting his views at the press conference when a scuffle broke out. He said he did not see what happened over the chair. Brijesh Gautam said that national president Akhilesh Yadav would be informed about the incident. Further action would be taken after a decision by the national leadership. The district president rejected Anshuman Singh's claim that he had been invited personally. He said all leaders had been informed in the group and invited. Anshuman Singh releases video, says incident is being given a political colour At around 10:30 p.m. on Saturday, Anshuman Singh released a video on social media, giving his side of the story on the entire matter. Accusing Nagina Sahni, he said that she did not want the Samajwadi Party to develop. Referring to the Rural Assembly constituency, Anshuman said that on a seat where there was a BJP wave, he had forced the BJP to think. This was why Nagina Sahni was परेशान. Linking the entire controversy to his political image, he accused Nagina Sahni and said that the incident was being given a political colour. Preparations to rebuild the organisation from scratch After the organisation was dissolved, the Samajwadi Party will now have to rebuild its organisation in Gorakhpur. New appointments will be made, from the district and metropolitan presidents to office-bearers of various frontal organisations. The party leadership's decision is being seen as a stern message to the Gorakhpur organisation over discipline and internal infighting.

stories.title: Owaisi says, ‘We have conveyed our point to Akhilesh’:Cites Bihar example; Shaukat says SP will be reduced to 27 seats in 2027
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi targeted SP chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on Sunday. He said, "The SP chief is troubled by what we say. We say that we will not lay out carpets and that we are not a vote bank. We should get our due. We say that Muslims should have a political agency. Clearly, those who do not accept this reality must be troubled by it." On an alliance with the SP, Owaisi said, "Our party has made its position clear. We have also given Bihar as an example. Whatever alliance is formed, you will be informed." Owaisi did not reveal his cards for now on the possibility of an alliance with Akhilesh Yadav. He had arrived in Lucknow on Sunday to address a public meeting in Shravasti. He made these remarks while speaking to journalists at the airport. Meanwhile, AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali made a major statement. He said, “If an alliance is formed in which there is no Muslim leadership and AIMIM is not included, then it is not an alliance but a betrayal. Such an alliance will exploit the oppressed, Muslim, deprived and exploited sections of society.” SP gave a ticket to the son of the very person who defeated the INDIA alliance Asaduddin Owaisi, chief of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen, or AIMIM, also took a dig at Akhilesh Yadav over the Samajwadi Party's Rajya Sabha nomination. He said that in Jharkhand, the son of the BJP-backed candidate who defeated the INDIA alliance candidate in the election has now been given a ticket. He questioned why AIMIM alone is accused of being the BJP's 'B team' when such decisions are taken. Owaisi said, “The SP made such a person its candidate, even though he is the president of the Gujarat Cricket Association. In Gujarat, the cricket board is viewed as a political board. Understand this... Cross-voting takes place in the INDIA alliance. The INDIA alliance candidate loses in Jharkhand, and now they give his son a ticket. Understand this dynastic politics that is going on too...” Owaisi said, ‘Try fielding someone else from Saharanpur’ Owaisi said that Imran Masood had been appointed the Uttar Pradesh Congress working president, asking why he was being associated with the party. He said, "Field someone else from Saharanpur and get them elected; then you will know." Owaisi had issued an ultimatum until 2 October
