stories.title: ‘BJP district chief raped me, recorded video, threatened me’:Party leader in Ballia alleges; claims he got his name removed from FIR
stories.summary: In Ballia, a woman BJP leader has accused her own party's district president of rape. She claimed that Ballia district president Sanjay Mishra raped her and made an obscene video. He then threatened to make the video viral and had his associates rape her as well. When she protested after becoming fed up with the harassment, her videos were made viral. The woman leader, who described herself as a member of the BJP district working committee, said, "When I reached the Kotwali to file a complaint, the police kept putting it off for 15 days. An FIR was later registered on 15 September after I complained to senior officials. However, Sanjay Mishra used his influence to have his name removed from the FIR. Less serious sections were also invoked against the other accused." The woman said, "As no action had been taken even after so many days, I decided to approach the media and seek help. District president Sanjay Mishra, district minister Alok Singh Monu, and their associates Ganesh Gupta and Ajit Mishra Chandan intimidated and exploited me for a long time. When it became unbearable, I began protesting." See 2 pictures- "I gave my statement at the Kotwali along with an affidavit" The woman said, "I gave my statement at the Kotwali along with an affidavit. I am not merely making allegations. This is the truth. They have ruined the lives of several women like me. But no one had the courage to come forward and speak out. That is why I have come forward." The woman said, "Sanjay Mishra has turned his office into a hub of exploitation. As a party worker, I visit the office. He subjected me to mental, financial and physical exploitation. Alok Singh Monu is his patron. He oversees all the extortion operations." 'Had his name removed from the case because he is influential' The woman said the district president is very influential. "I had named him, but he called the police station and had himself removed from the case. I appeal to the leaders of my party to help me get justice. This is not a fight I am facing alone. Many women cannot come forward because of fear." Sanjay Mishra said - It is not right to play with someone's character BJP district president Sanjay Mishra said that all the allegations made were baseless. “I am an ordinary party worker. I do not know whose instigation or what plan led to these allegations being made against me. She is saying that misconduct was committed, so she should give the date. It is not right to play with someone's character. I am the target today; tomorrow, it could be someone else. Such things are not good for a healthy democratic tradition,” Mishra said.

stories.title: Canter-trailer collide on Agra highway:People rush with buckets to loot oil
stories.summary: A diesel tanker collided with a trailer on a highway in Agra on Saturday morning, causing its tank to burst and fuel to spill onto the road. Soon after the accident, local residents reached the spot with buckets, cans and other containers and started collecting the spilled diesel. The accident took place in the Etmadpur police station area at around 7:45 am. The tanker was travelling towards Rasulabad in Firozabad when the trailer, coming from Firozabad towards Agra, hit it from behind near Fateh Singh’s culvert. According to the tanker operator, Shivdatt, the tanker had been filled with petrol and diesel at the Indian Oil depot in Etmadpur. It had two chambers, carrying 3,000 litres of petrol and 9,000 litres of diesel. The impact damaged the tanker’s fuel tank, causing diesel to leak onto the road. The loss in the accident is estimated at around ₹3-4 lakh. Check out the visuals below : A large crowd gathered at the spot after the fuel started leaking. Several people brought buckets, cans and other containers and were seen collecting the spilled diesel. A video of the incident has also surfaced. Tanker removed with a crane According to police, the fuel leak caused chaos at the spot. Traffic on the highway also came to a standstill. Police reached the spot, moved the crowd away and took control of the situation. The tanker was later removed from the road with the help of a crane. The spilled petrol and diesel also created a fire risk. As a precaution, police cleared the area and then restored traffic. Fortunately, no one was injured in the accident.

stories.title: Gandhi-Shastri Jayanti celebrated in Varanasi:Students spread message of truth, non-violence and ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’
stories.summary: Jatpur PG College in Varanasi celebrated the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, and the 122nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri on 2 October. A flag-hoisting ceremony was held on the college campus on the occasion. Principal Prof. Anil Pratap Singh hoisted the flag to inaugurate the programme. After this, garlands and floral tributes were offered to portraits of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri. The principal said that Gandhi's principles of truth, non-violence and cleanliness, as well as Shastri's slogan "Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan", remained relevant to young people even today. He called upon the students to adopt the ideals of both great leaders in their lives. The students shared their views on the lives and thoughts of Gandhi and Shastri and presented poems. College professors and students were present at the programme. It concluded with the national anthem.

stories.title: Gorakhpur woman elopes with lover, marries him:Abandoned at parents’ home after pregnancy; husband threatens to burn her alive, FIR filed
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a young man eloped with a girl from his village, married her and took her to Karnataka. Later, when she became pregnant, he refused to keep her with him. The man allegedly brought the girl back to her parental home and abandoned her there. He threatened to douse her with petrol and set her on fire if she returned to him. Her in-laws are also refusing to keep her in their home. Based on the victim's complaint, an FIR was registered at Jhangha police station on Friday. The police are investigating the matter and taking further action. Here is the full case... A young woman from the Jhangha police station area stated in her complaint that three years ago, a young man from her village lured her into a trap, eloped with her and married her at the Gorakhnath Temple. After the marriage, he took her with him to Karnataka. Everything was going well, but after four months, when he learnt that his wife was pregnant, he began refusing to keep her with him. After a quarrel, he brought her back to her parental home and abandoned her there. The victim has been living at her father's house ever since. It is alleged that when the young woman went to her in-laws' home, the people there also opposed her and drove her away, refusing to let her stay in the house. According to the victim, when she insisted on staying, her mother-in-law, father-in-law and sister-in-law together pulled her by the hair and beat her. In-laws pulled her hair and assaulted her It is alleged that they threatened to sprinkle petrol on her and burn her alive if she returned there. They also allegedly threatened to implicate the victim's brother in false cases and kill her father. The woman said that she wanted to live with her husband. Where would she go with her child? Jhangha police station in-charge Gyanendra Singh said an FIR had been registered against five people, including the woman's husband, based on her written complaint. Police are investigating the case. Further action will be taken based on the findings.

stories.title: DM inspects CM Grid road late at night:Deadline to finish work by October 30; action against litterers
stories.summary: Roads in Kanpur will be repaired before Diwali, and sanitation arrangements will also be improved. The administration has begun preparations for this. District Magistrate Mahendra Singh Tanwar inspected several areas of the city late on Friday night. Municipal Commissioner Arpit Upadhyay and CDO Abhinav J. Jain accompanied him. The CM Grid road work near Deep Cinema in Zone 3 was found to be progressing slowly. The District Magistrate expressed displeasure and directed that the road work be completed by 30 October at all costs. Deadline of 30 October to complete the work During the inspection, the executing agency said that this approximately 1.8-km-long road had been approved under the second phase of the CM Grid project. The project's second instalment of ₹924.84 lakh was approved in September 2026. Drainage and utility-related work is also being carried out on the road. The executing agency had sought time until November to complete the work, but the District Magistrate shortened the deadline and issued an ultimatum to complete the construction by 30 October. He also assessed the quality of the white-topping work. Waste disposal arrangements also inspected at Gaushala Crossing in Juhi After garbage was found on the road, the officials inspected the Garbage Vulnerable Point (GVP) near Gaushala Crossing. The officials said that earlier, large quantities of garbage would accumulate there and spread on to the road. Now, the garbage is being collected on a designated platform and sent to the transfer station. The District Magistrate directed that under no circumstances should garbage spread on to the road. For this, staff should be deployed as required, and action should also be taken against those who dump garbage in public places. Instructions issued not to compromise on quality in road construction After this, PCTS and GVP in the Juhi area were also inspected. The District Magistrate directed officials to ensure regular waste collection, monitoring of the sites and improved sanitation arrangements. In view of Diwali and other festivals, officials were asked to conduct special cleanliness drives on major roads, in markets and at public places. Instructions were also issued to arrange waste collection in two shifts, as required, so that rubbish does not accumulate on the roads. The District Magistrate asked officials to conduct regular inspections and monitor the quality of road construction and sanitation arrangements.

stories.title: 7-hour traffic block at Lucknow station today:Work from 10am-5pm; platforms changed for 15 trains
stories.summary: A seven-hour traffic block will be in effect at Lucknow railway station from 10 am to 5 pm on 3 October (today). Essential track-related work will be carried out at the station during this period. As a result, the platforms for around 15 trains will be changed. Railways has asked passengers to check the platform information before boarding their trains. According to Northern Railway, repair and renewal work on the diamond double-slip point between Lucknow and LBH will be carried out on the north line of the Lucknow East Changing Yard. As a result, train operations on platforms 1, 2, 3, MR-1 and 9 will be affected. Trains will operate from the south-side platforms 4 to 8. Seven trains from Platform 1 to be shifted Seven trains operating from Platform 1 will operate from platforms 5 and 7. These include the Amritsar-Howrah, Anand Vihar Terminal-Ayodhya Cantt Vande Bharat, Yeshwantpur-Gorakhpur, Meerut City-Varanasi, Jammu Tawi-Guwahati, Lucknow-Kanpur Central and Howrah-Amritsar trains. Two trains on Platform 2 also shifted The Dhanbad-Firozpur Cantt train, which departs from Platform 2, will now depart from Platform 5. Meanwhile, the Jammu Tawi-Kolkata Terminal train will depart from Platform 4. The railway has asked passengers to check the display boards and announcements after reaching the station because of the platform changes, so that they do not face any difficulty catching their train.

On seeing the flames rising, local residents reached the spot and informed the police. Police and fire brigade teams then reached the scene. Firefighters tried to bring the blaze under control The fire in both vehicles was so intense that firefighters had to make strenuous efforts to put it out. Police sent one of the drivers injured in the accident to hospital for treatment. Traffic affected on highway Vehicle movement on the highway was affected by the accident. Police are investigating the cause of the accident.

stories.title: Parents refuse to meet ‘blue-drum’ Muskan:Won’t let her meet daughter before sentence; won’t seek bail
stories.summary: We do not want to meet Muskan. Nor do we want Pihu to meet her. We do not want her to have a negative influence on Pihu. Our entire family has been under immense stress for the past one-and-a-half years. We have somehow managed to stay alive. Now, we are trying to bring our lives back on track. We neither want to meet Muskan nor apply for her bail. Muskan’s parents in Meerut said this in a phone conversation with Dainik Bhaskar. Seventeen months ago, Muskan, along with her lover Sahil, allegedly killed her husband Saurabh Rajput. They packed his dismembered body in a blue drum and covered it with cement and sand. The court has now held Muskan and Sahil guilty. The court will pronounce the sentence on October 14. Before the sentencing, Muskan has expressed her desire to meet her seven-and-a-half-year-old daughter Pihu and her parents. Here is what Muskan’s parents said about it... Muskan pressuring us Muskan’s father Pramod Rastogi said, “We will not go to meet Muskan. We do not want to meet her either. Similarly, Muskan’s mother Kavita Rastogi said, “We do not want to meet Muskan. We have not even thought about meeting her. However, we have learnt that Muskan herself is insisting on meeting us. “If the court asks us to meet Muskan, we will have to go and meet her while following the law. We will consider it if that happens. However, we do not want to meet Muskan on our own. We are helpless ourselves. We also have to take care of our children and family. “Wherever we go, people start troubling us. Parents are parents. Muskan may not have learnt to love us, but we are still her parents.” We will not let Muskan’s shadow fall on Pihu Kavita said, “Muskan’s daughter Pihu is living with us. There is no question of letting Pihu meet her. We do not want even her shadow to fall on Pihu. Pihu is a small child and she is already very disturbed because she misses her mother and father. “We cannot make her more distressed by making her meet Muskan. It will only have a bad effect on the child. If the court asks us to do so, we will have to take her to meet her. Muskan is, after all, her mother, but all this is mental trauma for Pihu.” Pihu cries even when she sees Saurabh’s photo Kavita said, “Pihu misses her mother and father a lot. Whenever she sees Muskan or Saurabh’s photo on a mobile phone, in a newspaper or on TV, she starts crying. Even if I look at a photo of Muskan or Saurabh and Pihu sees me, she stops me. She says, ‘Nani, don’t look at this.’ “The child spends her entire day distressed. She says, ‘Nani, let’s go back to our old house.’ This is our new house. We bought it only three years ago. Before that, we lived in a rented house for 10 years. “Pihu has been with us since the beginning. She grew up in that house, which is why she misses her old home a lot. She misses her father terribly. She goes to the terrace and talks to the stars. She says hi and hello to them.” It is difficult for us to step out Kavita said, We do not want to say anything to anyone anymore. YouTubers have ruined our lives. It has become difficult for us to step out of our house. Whenever we go outside, YouTubers record our videos and upload them. They say all kinds of things about us. This has made our lives even more difficult.We do not want to appear in front of cameras. After all, we also have to look after our other children. Their entire future is at stake. That is why we wanted to sell our house and move to another city. We wanted to give our children a new life there. But people portrayed even that in a very wrong way. They said we were planning to sell our house for reasons best known to us. We have received no call from Saurabh’s family Kavita said, “We are very simple people. I do not know how everything went so wrong. Even now, we do not have the heart to apply for Muskan’s bail. Our minds are not working. We are completely broken. Our entire family is in shock. “Muskan’s father is also very unwell. He has been under a lot of stress for the past year. The things we want to forget and move on from are repeatedly brought back to us. People keep troubling us and do not let us come out of our grief.” She added that they have not received any call from Saurabh’s family so far.

stories.title: Why Ajay Rai was removed as UP Congress chief:Aradhana is Brahmin face, has good chemistry with Akhilesh; Imran to woo Muslims
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Congress leadership has made a major political move. Ajay Rai has been removed as state president, and Aradhana Misra ‘Mona’ has been given charge of the party’s Uttar Pradesh unit. Imran Masood has been appointed working president, while Devendra Prasad Mehra and Alok Prasad have been made vice-presidents. Through these four appointments, the Congress has sought to create a new and balanced ‘Brahmin-Muslim-OBC-Dalit’ social equation in Uttar Pradesh. The changes are being seen not just as an organisational reshuffle, but as part of the party’s electoral roadmap. New faces and strategy of social balance Imran Masood to strengthen the Muslim equation By appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president, the party has sought to send a clear message to Muslim voters in western Uttar Pradesh as well as across the state, with the aim of retaining this support within the Congress-SP alliance. Devendra Prasad Mehra to reach out to Nishad voters Devendra Prasad Mehra, who belongs to the Nishad community and has influence in eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bundelkhand, has been appointed vice-president. The move is aimed at making inroads into the Nishad support base associated with the BJP, represented by Sanjay Nishad, as well as the Samajwadi Party. Alok Prasad to strengthen Dalit leadership Alok Prasad, who comes from the Dalit community, has also been appointed vice-president. The move gives the party a prominent Dalit face in the state. Rahul Gandhi backs UP in-charge’s social-equation strategy UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam had already presented the argument for a social equation before the party high command. He had pointed out that Ajay Rai belongs to the Bhumihar community, whose population in the state is relatively small. According to Gautam’s argument, the Congress needs a leader with a larger and broader support base to win the 2027 elections. Gautam himself belongs to the Dalit community. His strategy is to take on Uttar Pradesh through a Dalit-Brahmin or Dalit-OBC combination. As part of this reshuffle, the party approved the appointment of MLA Aradhana Misra, daughter of senior leader Pramod Tiwari, as state president. Differences with UP in-charge became a setback for Ajay Rai Ajay Rai had been the state president for around three years. During this period, he travelled to different districts of the state to strengthen the organisation. After the Congress replaced Brahmin leader Avinash Pandey with Dalit leader Rajendra Pal Gautam as its UP in-charge, differing positions began to emerge between Rai and Gautam. Here are two such instances: 1. Different positions on seat-sharing with SP Gautam became more active in the party’s strategy on seat-sharing with the Samajwadi Party. He advocated negotiations with the SP for an equal number of seats. Rai, meanwhile, repeatedly stressed the need to prepare the organisation across all 403 Assembly constituencies in Uttar Pradesh. 2. Rai unhappy over Gautam’s attempt to meet Mayawati In May 2026, Rajendra Pal Gautam suddenly went to BSP chief Mayawati’s residence to meet her. Some other Congress leaders and MPs also accompanied him. However, Mayawati did not meet them. Rai openly expressed his displeasure over the incident. He said, I have no information about whose permission Gautam went to Mayawati’s house. Ajay Rai’s individual performance did not help There was an argument in favour of retaining Ajay Rai as state president based on the party’s strong performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The biggest point in Rai’s favour was that the party won six Lok Sabha seats under his leadership. He himself gave Prime Minister Narendra Modi a close contest in Varanasi and led during a total of seven rounds at different stages of the counting. However, the party did not retain Rai despite his individual electoral performance.

stories.title: Drought in 17 districts, rainfall deficit up to 68%:‘Severe’ in Jaunpur, Shamli, Ghaziabad; what will be impact across state?
stories.summary: The monsoon season is over. Uttar Pradesh has received 8% more rainfall than normal. Despite this, 17 districts are facing the possibility of drought. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered a survey on September 30. Based on the report, these districts could be declared drought-hit by October 31. So, what impact will drought in 17 districts have on the rest of Uttar Pradesh? What is the government process for declaring an area drought-hit? Read the UP Explainer... Question 1: What are the criteria and process for declaring an area drought-hit? Answer: A shortage of rainfall alone is not enough to declare an area drought-hit. The Agriculture Department, Meteorological Department, and revenue officials assess crop damage, rainfall deficiency, and soil moisture in the affected area. The process involves three steps... Step 1: The extent of rainfall deficiency in the area is assessed. A 25% or more deficiency in rainfall is considered the first indicator of drought. Step 2: The impact of low rainfall on agriculture is assessed. This includes examining the area under cultivation, satellite mapping, and the condition of rivers, ponds, and other water bodies in the area. Step 3: A report is prepared on crop damage in at least 10% of the villages in the affected tehsil or district. Crop damage of 50% or more is considered a ‘severe drought’. Question 2: What is the situation in UP right now? Answer: This year, the monsoon rainfall situation has been quite contrasting across Uttar Pradesh and the country. Due to the uneven rainfall pattern, UP is facing a dual crisis of floods and drought. While 38 districts, nearly half the state, have received normal or above-normal rainfall, farmers in the remaining 37 districts are awaiting government relief under drought criteria. Question 3: How could drought affect UP’s supply chain? Answer: The impact of drought in 17 districts will not remain limited to these areas. It could trigger a chain reaction across the state’s food supply system and economy. Question 4: What changes after an area is declared drought-hit? Answer: Once the government declares a district or tehsil drought-affected, the entire administrative machinery shifts into ‘disaster management mode’. The changes can be understood in five points.

stories.title: मायावती ने फिर जताया भतीजे पर भरोसा, कांशीराम जयंती के मंच से आकाश आनंद की वापसी का बड़ा ऐलान

stories.title: BJP Rajya Sabha Candidate: राज्यसभा टिकट मिलने के बाद प्रकाश पाल का सपा पर पलटवार, बोले- अब PDA का मतलब ‘पैसा देने वाले आओ’

stories.summary: प्रेमानंद महाराज का बाल भक्त मयंक प्रयागराज में मिल गया है। उसके परिवारवालों के मुताबिक पिछले 57 दिन से वे उसे तलाश रहे थे। मयंक के माथे पर लेपन और गले में राधा कंठी है। प्रयागराज में पुलिस ने उसे उसके मामा को सौंप दिया। 57 दिन बाद मयंक के ननिहाल पहुंचने पर परिवार में खुशी की लहर दौड़ गई है।

stories.title: Azam’s wife Tanzeen Fatima says Akhilesh is like my son:Why pressure for 15 seats? SP chief will visit Rampur soon
stories.summary: Tanzin Fatima, wife of Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan denied reports that Azam had sent a list of 15 candidates to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav from jail on Monday. Speaking at a press conference in Rampur, she said the letter she had taken to Akhilesh did not mention any demand for 15 seats. She said, “I had gone carrying Azam sahib's letter, and the claim that the letter demanded 15 seats is completely false.” Fatima said Azam Khan considers Akhilesh Yadav like his own child. “He is like my child too. The claim that he would send a letter to his own child to put pressure on him is beyond comprehension. We had gone to discuss our personal issues with him. It was a family meeting. There was no discussion about any seat or who would contest the election.” A national newspaper claimed on 3 October that Azam Khan had sent a list of 15 names to party president Akhilesh Yadav from Rampur jail. It claimed that Azam had named his preferred contenders for 15 Assembly seats in Rampur, Sambhal, Moradabad, Saharanpur, Meerut and Badaun in western Uttar Pradesh. Former Rajya Sabha MP Tazeen Fatima arrived in Lucknow with her elder son, Adeeb Azam, on Wednesday, 30 September. She met Akhilesh Yadav and handed him the list. Tazeen later described it as a courtesy meeting and refused to provide any information about the list. The report said differences over tickets had emerged between Akhilesh Yadav and Azam Khan in the past as well. Despite Azam's objection, the Samajwadi Party fielded Maulana Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Akhilesh Yadav also campaigned in his support. About Tanjin... The newspaper should state who those trusted sources were who provided this information and allowed it to be published without establishing whether the news was true or false. People read the news published in newspapers, and it also shapes public opinion. This raises the question of whether the news being conveyed to the public is true or false. Akhilesh Yadav has said that he will meet Azam Khan. Whenever Akhilesh can make time, he may come to meet him within the next two to four days. Asked about meeting Swami Prasad Maurya, Tanzeen Fatima said that she had only met him as a courtesy. There was no political discussion of any kind. Newspapers write something or the other about the ED and Income Tax every day. It seems as though the ED is not conducting the investigation and the newspapers themselves are carrying it out. We are fully co-operating, whether it is an ED investigation or an Income Tax investigation. Azam serving a 10-year sentence with his son Abdullah Azam Khan faces 104 cases. So far, sentences have been handed down in eight cases. He is serving a 10-year sentence in Rampur jail alongside his son, Abdullah Azam. Both were convicted in a case involving two PAN cards. Meanwhile, Rampur's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust associated with it are also under investigation. The Enforcement Directorate has begun investigating a case related to the trust's bank transactions.

stories.title: No car in dowry, wife abandoned at crossing:Man gives triple talaq in Aligarh, remarries; wife alleges affair with transgender person
stories.summary: A woman in Etah accused her husband of giving her triple talaq after he allegedly did not receive a car in dowry on Monday. He first beat her and then brought her to Aligarh, where he abandoned her at a crossroads. Her family kept waiting for the matter to be settled, but meanwhile, the accused husband remarried. After learning about her husband's second marriage, the woman lodged a complaint with the police. She also accused her husband of having an affair with a transgender person in Delhi. The police registered an FIR against five people, including her husband. The case is from the Kotwali Nagar area. Family arranged only daughter's wedding with great pomp Subhan Saifi, a resident of Rewari Mohalla, works as a steel labourer. He has four sons—Mohammad Kaif, Mohammad Faiz, Mohammad Saif and Mohammad Jaif—and an only daughter, Mantasha Saifi (28). All four sons help their father in his work. On December 3, 2025, Subhan married Mantasha to Sharik Saifi, a resident of Aligarh. Sharik works as an AC repair technician in Delhi. Subhan organised the wedding on a large scale and gave ₹5 lakh in cash, along with jewellery and other dowry items. As soon as Mantasha reached her in-laws' house after the wedding, her in-laws allegedly started demanding a car. THusband brought her from Aligarh and left her at a crossing About two and a half months after the wedding, on February 15, Sharik and his family members allegedly put Mantasha in a vehicle and brought her to Etah. They made her get out at Ali Mohammad Chowk. Sharik then allegedly said, "Talaq, talaq, talaq" three times. Mantasha's family repeatedly pleaded with Sharik's family, but they did not agree to take her back. Her father, Subhan, alleges that Sharik has since married another woman. In-laws used to taunt her Mantasha said that she was married to Sharik from Aligarh. Despite her father having an injured eye, her family gave ₹5 lakh at the wedding. But some time after the wedding, her in-laws would taunt her and ask, "What did you bring from your family?" They would also ask when she would bring a car. At the instigation of my mother-in-law, Shameem Bano, my husband, Sharik, would also assault me. My father-in-law, Naeem Akhtar, often came home after drinking. He would come and sit in my room. He would stare at me and speak rudely to me about not bringing a car. Accuses husband of being in contact with a transgender person The woman said her husband works as an AC and refrigerator technician in Delhi's Shaheen Bagh and is in contact with a transgender person named Komal. She alleged that he followed Komal's advice, stopped talking to her and refused to live with her. She said her husband later told her, “talaq, talaq, talaq” three times and left her at Ali Mohammad intersection. Father says daughter's in-laws were driven by greed Her father, Subhan Saifi, alleged that his daughter's in-laws had been demanding a car from the beginning. He said he gave ₹5 lakh in cash, an AC, a fridge, gold and silver jewellery, and other items according to his means. He said the in-laws also humiliated around 60 family members when they went to invite them, refusing to provide breakfast or water and serving leftover food late at night after the guests had left. Did not relent even after several panchayat meetings Subhan said several people tried to settle the matter during panchayat meetings, but the groom's family did not agree. He alleged that they gave his daughter triple talaq, pushed her out and left her at a crossroads before arranging the man's second marriage. He also accused the husband, his sister, brother-in-law and parents-in-law of harassing his daughter. Subhan said he had not named anyone innocent in the complaint. He said he has four sons and only one daughter, and spent all his savings on her wedding. He also took a bank loan and borrowed money from his brothers, which he is still repaying. He demanded punishment for those responsible and justice for his daughter.

stories.summary: Cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi put in a strenuous practice session at Ekana Stadium a day before the clash with the West Indies. While practising on Monday, he hit 15 sixes in an hour. During the session, three shots also went up in the air as catches. Bowling coach Morne Morkel had the pace bowlers bowl to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Vaibhav played his fastest shots towards mid-on and mid-off. On Monday, the India and West Indies teams spoke to the media about their preparations. India's bowling coach Morkel said that their focus would be on winning the series opener. The young players are under scrutiny. The West Indies, meanwhile, were represented at the briefing by their star spinner. He said that they were not afraid and that what had happened was in the past. Everyone knows how formidable the West Indies are in T20 cricket When a Bhaskar reporter congratulated West Indies player Akeal Hosein on his 100th T20 International, he smiled and said that he had played only 99 matches so far. His 100th match would be recorded after he took the field in the playing XI. Speaking about his previous record against India, he said that what had happened was in the past. "We are not afraid of India. We will not back down from the West Indies' aggressive approach in T20 cricket. They described bowling in the powerplay as challenging and said matches cannot be won by relying solely on data. It is crucial to make immediate decisions on the field after assessing the pitch, the wind direction and the match situation. He said, “I want to become the world's number one T20 bowler.” Morkel targeting victory and giving new players a chance India's bowling coach Morne Morkel outlined the team management's vision. He said winning every match was the priority, but at the same time, new and young players would be given a full opportunity to showcase their talent. Speaking about the players' long journey after the Asian Games, Morkel said there was some fatigue, but the team would take the field with full energy as the series began. With the upcoming T20 World Cup in mind, the team management's aim is to build a strong pool of players. Mayank Yadav's return and faith in all-rounders Morkel expressed happiness at fast bowler Mayank Yadav's return from injury and praised his X-factor. He also said that giving youngsters such as Prince Yadav experience at international level was important for Indian cricket. Among the batters, he praised Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma and Suryakumar Yadav for their ability to change their batting positions and take responsibility. In addition, Shivam Dube and Nitish Reddy are being viewed as extra bowling options, while Kuldeep Yadav's return to rhythm in the spin department is being seen as a major plus for the Indian team.

stories.title: Fire breaks out during bike repair in Ghatampur:Short circuit sparks blaze; mechanic douses it with soil
stories.summary: A fire suddenly broke out during repairs at a bike repair shop in Ghatampur, Kanpur, on Monday afternoon. As the fire started, the Passion Pro motorcycle inside the shop began burning fiercely. The sudden flames caused panic at the scene. The mechanic and local residents began trying to extinguish the fire by throwing soil on it. The fire was brought under control after considerable effort. Fortunately, no one was injured in the incident. On Monday, a mechanic was repairing a Passion Pro motorcycle at the Salamate Hind Gharib Nawaz bike repair shop near Teen Number in the Ghatampur police station area. According to the mechanic, a short circuit suddenly occurred while he was working on the motorcycle's wiring. The motorcycle then caught fire. Before long, the flames engulfed several parts of the motorcycle. A sudden fire broke out in the bike, causing panic among people near the shop. On seeing the flames, people rushed towards the spot. The mechanic, with the help of local residents, immediately began trying to extinguish the fire. As water was not available, people tried to bring the fire under control by throwing soil on it. The fire was put out after considerable effort. However, by then, the bike's engine, seat, wiring and other parts had been badly burnt and damaged. After the fire was extinguished, the bike was taken out of the shop. A crowd gathered at the spot after the incident. Local residents said the fire was extinguished in time; otherwise, the other goods inside the shop could also have caught fire. Fortunately, the mechanic and people nearby escaped safely amid the flames. No one was reported to have suffered burns in the incident. Prima facie, a short circuit in the bike's wiring is being cited as the cause of the fire.

stories.title: Work stops at school flagged by Divya Mittal:Villagers oppose project in Mirzapur; Forest Dept says land belongs to it
stories.summary: The construction of an upper primary school in Lahuriyadah village of Mirzapur’s Haliya area was stopped by the Forest Department on October 4, leading to anger among villagers. The school was being built with the permission of former IAS officer Divya Mittal. The Forest Department claimed that the land belonged to it and said construction there was illegal. A Forest Department team also took away equipment, including spades and carrying pans, from the masons and labourers who were working on the foundation. Earlier, on September 30, Haliya Block Education Officer Prakash Chandra Yadav and village administrator Kaushalendra Gupta reached Lahuriyadah village with a team. After demarcating the land for the school, they started the construction work. However, the Forest Department stopped the work on the fifth day. Patwari says school is being built on gram sabha land There are conflicting claims by the Revenue and Forest departments over the land allotted for the school. Patwari Nikhil Pathak said plot number 1116 G, measuring 0.169 hectares or around 13 biswa, was allotted for the school. He said the land belongs to the gram sabha and the Revenue Department. He said that despite this, the Forest Department was claiming the land. Senior officials have been informed about the matter. Meanwhile, Drummondganj Ranger Ravishankar Sharma said the land in Lahuriyadah village where the upper primary school was being built belongs to the Forest Department. He said construction was stopped for this reason. Forest Department map shows land as Revenue Department’s According to the ranger, the school was being built on plot numbers 730 and 732, as shown in the Forest Department’s map. He said that in the Forest Department’s map for Fasli 1359, plot number 733 is recorded as Revenue Department land, and the school can be built there. The ranger alleged that the Revenue Department team did not contact the Forest Department before allotting land for the school. He said land under the Forest Department was allotted for the construction. Villagers, who are upset over the construction being stopped, said there were no trees or plants on the land where the school was being built. They questioned why the construction work was stopped. Villagers said - land should have been checked before building the school Villagers, including Heera Yadav, Chaurasia Devi, Rajkumar and Harilal, said that if the land belonged to the Forest Department, how did the tehsil administration allot it for the construction of a school? They have demanded an investigation into the entire matter. The land was demarcated and construction work started on September 30. However, just five days later, the Forest Department claimed that the land belonged to it and stopped the work. This has raised questions over the working of the tehsil administration and the Forest Department. Villagers said there should have been coordination between the departments concerned before the land was allotted for the school. They questioned why the matter was not checked before construction began if there was already a dispute over the land records. BSA said, “I have no information about this” Mirzapur BSA Anil Kumar Verma said he had no information about the construction work at Lahuriyadah Upper Primary School being stopped. He said the matter could be discussed with Halia BEO. According to information issued by the District Basic Education Officer on September 30, a proposal had been sent in 2024-25 to upgrade Primary School Lahuriyadah. In 2025-26, the State Project Director approved the proposal and allocated ₹25.58 lakh for the work. About three years ago, then District Magistrate Divya Mittal had approved the upgradation of the school in Lahuriyadah. Despite the budget being released in the 2025-26 session, construction work could not begin. The work had started only five days earlier. Former IAS officer Divya Mittal resigned a month ago It may be recalled that well-known Uttar Pradesh IAS officer Divya Mittal, 43, resigned from the service about a month ago. She was serving as Special Secretary in the Revenue Department in Lucknow. Divya sent her resignation to Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal. On Sunday morning, she announced her resignation in posts on Facebook and Instagram.

4 arrested with ₹50 crore drugs in Lucknow:Delhi Police bust factory; accused went to deliver heroin by car
stories.summary: Four people were arrested after Delhi Police’s Rohini district Special Staff busted an illegal heroin-making factory in Jankipuram, Lucknow on Monday. Police recovered 6.275 kg of processed heroin, chemicals and equipment used to make the drug from the factory. The four accused were allegedly linked to an interstate drug supply network. According to police, 7.076 kg of heroin was recovered in total, with an estimated international market value of around ₹50 crore. 6.275 kg heroin and chemicals recovered Based on technical surveillance, Delhi Police raided a house in Sita Colony, Jankipuram, on October 4, where heroin was allegedly being manufactured. Police arrested 35-year-old Bablu from the spot. Police recovered 6.275 kg of processed heroin, 2.504 kg of sodium, 787 grams of acetic anhydride, a mixer grinder, gas cylinder, weighing machine and utensils used in the manufacturing process. Operation started in Delhi and reached Lucknow, Bareilly According to police, the operation began on September 16 in Delhi’s Begumpur area. The Special Staff arrested 58-year-old Laxman Hooda, who had arrived in a Grand Vitara to deliver drugs. Police recovered 300 grams of heroin and ₹3 lakh in cash from him. During interrogation, Laxman revealed information about the network, following which 51-year-old Anil alias Bhola was arrested in Sonipat on September 17. Police recovered a Mahindra XUV-700 and 501 grams of heroin from him. Police said 12 cases had already been registered against Anil. He had also been declared a fugitive after jumping parole. Main supplier arrested after 120-km chase After Bablu’s arrest in Lucknow, police learnt about the network’s main supplier and the owner of the factory. A police team chased him for around 120 km and arrested Rukhsar Ali alias Raju in Bareilly on October 4. According to police, three cases have been registered against Rukhsar under the NDPS Act. One NDPS case has also been registered against Bablu, while Laxman is reportedly facing a murder case. Police probing money trail and supply network Deputy Commissioner of Police Rohini Shashank Jaiswal said the operation was carried out under the supervision of Inspector Sandeep Godara and ACP Ajmer Singh. Police are now investigating the network’s financial transactions, the supply of raw materials and other people linked to it. ‘Four Delhi Police personnel arrived around 3 am’ A local resident said four Delhi Police personnel arrived in the area around 3 am on Sunday. After carrying out the operation for about an hour, they arrested some people and took away the seized items. Later, local police also reached the spot. Delhi Police locked the house before leaving. According to residents, a man regularly lived in the house and a woman also visited him. Four or five other people frequently came there as well. Residents said they used vehicles such as Scorpios and Fortuners, and police caps could also be seen in these vehicles.

stories.title: Akash Anand becomes BSP national coordinator again after 25 days:Mayawati removed nephew thrice; gave post after father-in-law quit politics
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati has taken her nephew Akash Anand back into the party after 32 days. He has been made the National Coordinator on Monday. On October 2, Akash Anand shared an emotional post on social media platform X. He called Mayawati his political guru, inspiration and “Bua Maa”. He said that the BSP is his family and that he would not join any other party. He also supported his father-in-law Ashok Siddharth’s decision to retire from politics and said that “no relationship can be bigger than the mission and the party.” Explaining why he did not repost Mayawati’s post, Akash said he was away from social media at that time. He apologised for hurting anyone and asked for another chance to serve the party. The decision is believed to have been taken by Mayawati after getting feedback from BSP leaders. Akash’s removal had reportedly upset many young supporters of the party. Akash was removed even after father-in-law retired On September 9, Mayawati had said that if Ashok Siddharth retired from politics, she could consider restoring responsibilities to Akash. Akash did not repost Mayawati’s post. On September 10, Ashok Siddharth announced his retirement, but Mayawati considered the step late and completely removed Akash Anand from the party. Why was Akash Anand upset? Akash Anand was reportedly concerned over the BSP’s declining political strength. This was also seen when he gave Mayawati advice on the party’s funds. He reportedly said that the BSP had more than ₹650 crore in its party fund and suggested that the money should be used as much as possible to help candidates win the 2027 Assembly elections. However, Mayawati did not accept the suggestion. After this, a rally was held in Sadabad, Hathras, where Akash’s strong stand was widely praised. Soon after, reports said that Akash would also play an important role in deciding tickets this time. People from the rival group allegedly used this to create a problem and told Mayawati that the move was also being planned by Ashok Siddharth. Mayawati had taken action against Akash twice earlier as well. He was sidelined after being accused of being immature in politics. A meeting in Jewar had been planned without Mayawati’s approval, which had also upset her. It is said that Akash’s opponents presented the matter to Mayawati in a way that suggested he was taking all the decisions. After this, Mayawati ordered that her permission would be necessary for all future programmes involving Akash. Akash was also told to seek her permission before attending any such programme. The live telecast of the Jewar meeting was also not carried on the party’s official social media pages. This reportedly further increased Akash’s displeasure. He was then not invited to the party meetings held on August 25, August 31 and September 3. This time, Mayawati took action against Akash but did not clearly mention it in her official social media post. Akash later changed his social media bio, which was seen as confirmation of his removal from the party. In her September 9 post, Mayawati referred to Akash as Ashok Siddharth’s “son-in-law”. People close to Akash say that he was deeply hurt by the remark, as he felt it affected his self-respect. Ashok Siddharth also referred to this emotional issue in his post announcing his retirement from politics. Speaking about Akash, he said that Akash became his son-in-law later, but before that, he was Mayawati’s nephew and had a blood relationship with her.

stories.title: Woman caught stealing ghee, oil at Noida mall:Bag filled with 1kg packs; keeps face hidden from phone camera
stories.summary: A woman was caught stealing ghee and cooking oil at DLF Mall in Noida. A video of the incident has also emerged, showing the security team taking her away. The woman is seen using her mobile phone to hide her face. The woman had come to the mall shopping with her husband. She allegedly put ghee and cooking oil from a store into her bag without paying. She then left the mall with the items. The mall's security team caught her outside. The team asked her to have her bag checked, but she began arguing. The staff then checked the CCTV footage, which showed the woman putting the items in her bag. The security team then brought the woman back inside the mall. There, the staff told her in front of everyone that she had stolen the items. The woman later paid the bill for the items. The two sides then reached an agreement, and the matter was resolved. The incident took place on Sunday evening. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Sector 20 police station. See 2 pictures... Now, here are the details of the case DLF Mall is located in Sector 18, Noida, and has more than 300 stores. At around 7:30 p.m. on Sunday, a woman wearing a denim dress arrived at a store with her husband to shop. After some time, the woman left the store alone while her husband was having the items billed inside. As soon as she came out, a security guard stopped her and asked her to have her bag checked. The woman refused and began arguing with the security staff. When she did not show the bag for a long time, other security guards also arrived. Meanwhile, the store staff also came outside. The woman was stopped, and the CCTV footage was checked. The footage showed her placing a 1-kg container of ghee and a 1-kg bottle of oil in her bag. The staff then took the bag from the woman. A female security guard took her back inside the store. The staff removed the ghee and oil from the bag. The woman's husband was then also called inside. The store staff strongly reprimanded both of them in front of everyone. Now, know what is in the video In the video, a person says that two people were stealing goods worth ₹500-₹1,000 from the shop. The two were leaving with two bottles. They had stolen goods before as well. He then asks the mall staff what goods the two had stolen earlier. An employee says that the two had stolen ghee and other goods worth around ₹4,000. According to the employee, this was the fourth incident of theft. The two had been seen in the store four or five times. They were caught this time with the help of CCTV cameras. The employee also said that thefts had been reported since 15 August. However, they had not occurred continuously; such incidents took place at intervals of a few days. Dispute settled after payment The person in charge of the DLF outpost said a dispute had broken out between the woman and the security team over her taking the goods without paying. The woman later paid the bill for the goods. The two sides reached an agreement after the payment, and the matter was settled. Neither side has filed a complaint in the case.

stories.title: 'You should know when to open your mouth':SC slams Rajpal Yadav for failure to pay in cheque bounce case, says 'Your place is in jail'
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on 5 October strongly criticised Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav for failing to deposit ₹5 crore in connection with multiple cheque bounce cases. According to a Bar Bench report, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted that Rajpal Yadav had undertaken to deposit the amount with the Court registry by 5 October. However, he failed to do so. During the hearing in Rajpal Naurang Yadav Anr v. M/S Murli Projects Pvt Ltd, Yadav produced a copy of a ₹50 lakh demand draft and said that the amount was being processed by the bank. "Is this genuine or not? We don't know," the Bench remarked. Rajpal Yadav's counsel said the draft was with the bank and was being processed. ‘He is a film actor and acting here also’: Counsel Counsel appearing for Murli Projects accused the actor of showing disregard for the Court. "He is a film actor. He is acting here also. He has no respect for the majesty of the institution," the counsel said. When Rajpal's counsel argued that the complainants were not poor, Justice Bagchi strongly objected. ‘You should know when to open your mouth’: Judge "They may be richer than you, but they are poor to the extent you have swindled them. This arrogance needs to be put in its right place. You should know when to open your mouth. Your place is in jail," the judge said. Rajpal to make the payment by 6 October The Court directed Rajpal Yadav to make the payment by 6 October, Tuesday and listed the matter for hearing tomorrow as the first case. The dispute relates to ₹5 crore received by Rajpal and his wife from Murli Projects in connection with a film they were producing. After the film could not be completed within the agreed timeline, the parties entered into multiple agreements. Under one agreement, Rajpal issued eight security cheques to the company. A subsequent consent agreement provided for their return and the issuance of four fresh cheques of ₹10 crore each. Yadav, however, alleged that the earlier cheques were not returned and seven of them were presented and dishonoured. This led to criminal complaints against Yadav and his wife under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. In May 2024, a sessions court convicted Yadav and sentenced him to six months in jail. The Delhi High Court later suspended the sentence after he assured the Court that the dispute would be settled. However, the High Court subsequently noted that Rajpal had repeatedly failed to honour his payment commitments. In February 2026, he was directed to surrender and eventually surrendered on February 5. He was later granted interim relief after depositing ₹1.5 crore. The Supreme Court is now hearing his challenge to the three-month imprisonment order passed after he failed to make the remaining payments despite several undertakings.

stories.title: Slipper helps catch teacher couple’s killer:Woman saw him stealing at midnight; hacked her with axe along with friends in Sultanpur
stories.summary: The driver killed the teacher couple in Sultanpur on 28 September. He carried out the murders with the help of two friends. Around midnight, the driver was searching for the key to a cupboard in their room when the government school principal's wife saw him. When the woman scolded the driver, he objected and told her to keep quiet. However, she raised an alarm and called her husband. When the couple began to resist, the two men repeatedly struck them with a spade and an axe, killing them. After the murders, the accused fled with the money. Police arrested two accused at 1:15 pm on Monday and solved the case. One of their friends is still absconding. The incident took place at Manraji Educational Institution in Kumbhi Dadiya, Kadipur, around 55 km from the district headquarters. Two pictures related to the murders... Now read the entire incident in sequence... Mukesh Singh (45) has his ancestral home in Kumbhi Dadiya village. He was posted at the composite school in Khanuhat and was also the president of the block teachers' union. The principal's wife, Vinita (43), ran Manraghi Inter College from their home in the village, 1 km away. Her school has 17 teachers and staff members. Some 550 children study there. The couple's only son, Abhyuday (20), is studying at Delhi University. Accused also taught at the school while working as a driver SP Vineet Jaiswal said, "Rakesh Kumar Yadav (36), a resident of Kumbhi Dadiya, was the bus driver at the couple's school. He carried out the murder along with Ashish alias W Yadav (26) and a friend." The two were arrested about 50 metres before the big canal culvert near the Budhana bridge in Kadipur. Besides driving the bus at the teacher couple's school, Rakesh also taught computer science. Rakesh was in a poor financial condition. He therefore planned to steal from the institution with his neighbour and relative, Ashish Yadav. Driver said after being caught stealing: "I will not do it again" Rakesh had complete knowledge of the school, the office and the CCTV cameras installed there. He went to steal from the school office on the night of 28 September. Vinita Singh saw him while he was opening the locker and objected. The driver said he wanted to end the matter there with Vinita. He also said that he would not do anything like this again. But Vinita raised an alarm and called her husband, the principal. Fearing that his identity would be exposed, Rakesh then attacked Vinita with a spade kept nearby. When Mukesh, terrified after his wife's murder, tried to flee the room, Rakesh and Ashish chased him and killed him with an axe. They then fled with the money, mobile phone and Aadhaar card kept in the cupboard. Now read how the killer was caught because of a slipper Rakesh pretended to know nothing to avoid being charged with the murder of the teacher couple. He told the police that he had come to collect the bus key and had found the bodies of the husband and wife. During the investigation, the police found one of Rakesh's slippers at the scene. In addition to Rakesh, the police questioned 17 school staff members at different times. During questioning, the staff told the police that Rakesh wore slippers of that type. The police's suspicion of Rakesh then deepened. According to the police, Rakesh had damaged the school's CCTV cameras four days before the incident. He had also smashed the DVR. First misled the police, then broke down According to the SP, the links to the incident gradually fell into place. The accused's mobile location was also found at the school during the crime. An examination of his call details revealed that he had spoken to two friends. He was arrested today. Initially, he misled the police. When the police presented the evidence to him, he broke down. SP Vineet Jaiswal said: Police recovered the blood-stained spade used in the crime, one axe, ₹34,960, the Aadhaar card of the deceased Vinita Singh and the blood-stained clothes of the accused. One accused is absconding and a search is under way.

stories.title: All 8 BJP Rajya Sabha candidates in UP are new:Hardeep Puri, BL Verma excluded; Governor Gangwar’s daughter gets ticket
stories.summary: The BJP has announced candidates for eight Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh on Monday. Two of them are women. The BJP has nominated former Barabanki MP Priyanka Singh Rawat and Bareilly's Shruti Gangwar. Shruti is the daughter of Jharkhand Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar. She is currently the chairperson of Bareilly Urban Co-operative Bank Limited. Check out the list below : Find out the numbers needed to get a candidate elected if voting takes place The Uttar Pradesh Assembly has a total of 403 seats. At present, seven seats are vacant, leaving 396 MLAs. The formula to be used for the election to 10 Rajya Sabha seats will be 396/11+1. In other words, one will be added to the number obtained by dividing 396 by 11. This means 37 first-preference votes will be required to elect one member. If no additional candidates are fielded, the BJP will be able to get eight candidates and the Samajwadi Party two candidates elected unopposed. However, if an election is held, the arithmetic of either camp could be disrupted. In fact, the Samajwadi Party currently has only 100 MLAs. Of these, Ramakant Yadav is in jail, reducing the number to 99. It can comfortably get two candidates elected, but if it fields a third candidate, voting is certain. In such a situation, the Samajwadi Party will need at least 12 additional votes to get its third candidate elected. In this scenario, the BJP will need at least six additional votes to get its eighth candidate elected. If voting takes place, the threat of cross-voting will also emerge. In such a situation, the counting of second- and third-preference votes becomes crucial. For this, the MLAs are given proper training. They are told which candidate to place as their first preference and whom to place as their second and third preferences. Similarly, once a candidate reaches the prescribed quota during the counting, they are declared elected. About the SP candidates : Samajwadi Party candidate Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is the group president of Reliance Industries. He is considered close to well-known businessman Mukesh Ambani. He is also the president of the Gujarat Cricket Association. His father, Parimal Nathwani, is an Independent Rajya Sabha MP from Jharkhand. He reached the Rajya Sabha three months ago with the support of the NDA. The SP's other candidate, Prof. Ram Gopal Yadav, is Akhilesh Yadav's uncle. He has continuously represented the SP in the Rajya Sabha since the 1990s. He has also served once as a Lok Sabha MP. Ram Gopal Yadav is currently the party's principal general secretary as well.

stories.title: Youth dragged 50 metres with rope tied around neck:Beaten to death in Kanpur; father, daughters attack with iron rod
stories.summary: A young man was beaten to death in a land dispute in Kanpur Dehat. A video of the assault has also emerged, showing three women and two men beating the young man with sticks in the lane outside a house. When he was in a critical condition, one of the accused was seen tying a rope around his neck and dragging him. Family members hurriedly picked him up and sent him to the CHC, from where he was referred to Hallett Hospital in Kanpur. He died at 5 a.m. The incident took place at around 11.30 p.m. last Sunday in the Shivli police station area, about 30 km from the district headquarters. Watch two visuals Now understand the entire case in detail Ram Sanehi (28), son of Shiv Kumar, lived in Jurawarpur village in the Shivli police station area. He was married. His wife, Mamta, was living at her parents' home. It is alleged that he had been involved in a longstanding dispute with a family member, Ram Swaroop, over the wall of his house. Ram Sanehi drove an e-rickshaw. Villagers could not muster the courage to rescue him His sister Rajni said, "At around 11:30 p.m. on Sunday, Ram Swaroop, his wife Ramkumari, daughters Tannu, Reena and Priya, and son Ankush first abused my brother. When he objected, they began assaulting him. They then dragged him into the lane, where they repeatedly struck his head and legs with an iron pipe. Hearing the commotion, villagers reached the spot, but no one could muster the courage to rescue him." They kept beating him with an iron rod for half an hour The accused continued beating my brother for around half an hour. During this time, he was left in a critical condition. Ramswaroop tied a rope around my brother's neck and held on to him, while the others continued beating him. Later, they dragged him for 50 metres using the rope and threw him into a plot. According to Rajni, their father is elderly and was therefore unable to save her brother. He brought villagers to the spot, but the accused fled when they saw the crowd. The police then took him to Shivli CHC with the help of the villagers. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to Kanpur's Hallet Hospital as his condition was critical. Ramsanehi died at 5 a.m. on Monday. Fingers fractured, head split open According to his sister, the video shows that my brother was beaten like an animal. His head and the fingers of one hand were also split open. The marks left by being beaten with an iron pipe across his body had turned black.

stories.title: Video of Sant Premanand’s disciple emerges:Seen going to terrace before suicide; sandalwood paste on forehead, blood on dhoti
stories.summary: A third video recorded before Rasik Dulari Sharan's suicide in Vrindavan has emerged. The video shows Rasik Dulari walking up the stairs to the roof. Blood stains are visible on his dhoti. Twenty-five-year-old Rasik Dulari Sharan, who had taken initiation from Sant Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan, died by jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building on the morning of 25 September. His last rites were performed on the banks of the Yamuna on 26 September. In the case, police have questioned more than 30 people associated with Premanand Maharaj's Keli Kunj ashram. More than 50 disciples and volunteers associated with Premanand Maharaj's ashram live in the building. It is around 500 metres from Premanand Maharaj's old Keli Kunj ashram. Two days after the incident, CCTV footage emerged showing Rasik Dulari jumping from the fourth floor. A second video then emerged, showing him sitting on the boundary wall of the roof. Around six seconds later, he lies down on the floor. He then suddenly gets up and jumps over the boundary wall. Check out the pictures below : About the three videos First video: The first video of Rasik Dulari Sharan's suicide emerged on 27 September. It shows disciple Rasik Dulari Sharan suddenly falling feet-first onto the road from a height of 40 feet. His head hits the ground and splits open. He begins writhing in pain. Blood starts spreading across the road. Meanwhile, two cyclists happen to be passing by. One of them was a disciple dressed in yellow. Both are left shaken by the sight. A vehicle supplying water also arrives there at the same time. Second video: The second video of the suicide emerged on 3 October. It shows Rasik Dulari Sharan sitting on the roof's boundary wall. After six seconds, he lies down on the floor. He suddenly gets up and jumps from the boundary wall. Hearing the noise, another disciple runs to the spot and looks down. Third video: A third video surfaced on 5 October. In the 33-second video, Rasik Dulari Sharan is seen climbing the stairs to the roof. He is wearing a white dhoti and a white vest, with a yellow sheet draped over his body. Bloodstains can be seen on his dhoti. While climbing the stairs, he appears to be having some difficulty walking. It is being reported that the video was recorded as he was going to the roof before taking his own life. Full case details Rasik Dulari had been living for three months in the four-storey Guru Kripa Kunj building in the Rasik Dulari Varah Ghat area. He ended his life by jumping from the building's roof. According to the police, Rasik Dulari Sharan was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in critical condition, where he died. Eyewitnesses claimed that Rasik Dulari was bleeding from his private parts. A grinder with blood on it was found in the room. It is suspected that the disciple injured his private parts with the grinder. Post-mortem found cut marks on private parts Rasik Dulari Sharan Das's post-mortem was conducted by a panel of two doctors on 26 September. The procedure was also videographed. According to the preliminary report, injury marks were found on the head, legs and waist. Cut marks were also found on the private parts. After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to the family. Took initiation from Premanand Maharaj two years ago Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. He came to Vrindavan around two years ago and took initiation from Premanand Maharaj. He subsequently changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. He knew electrical work, so he was assigned this service at the ashram. Deepak was the second among two brothers and one sister. He had one elder sister, while his younger brother's name is Manish. Mother said, "We were not allowed to meet him" After being informed of her son Rasik Dulari's death, his mother, Laung Bai, said that she had last spoken to him two years ago. She was informed that her son had fallen, following which she rushed to Vrindavan. She said she had come to meet him before as well, but was not allowed to see him. She said God would take action against those responsible.

stories.title: VIDEO | 2 SP leaders clash at Agra meeting:Planning strategy against CEC Gyanesh Kumar; dispute over PDA Chaupal
stories.summary: A meeting of the Samajwadi Party was convened in Bah, Agra, on 7 October to plan a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. During the meeting, two leaders clashed. It was reported that an argument broke out between the two over the PDA Chaupal held in Jaitpur on 11 September. As the dispute escalated, it came close to turning physical. Party workers present at the meeting intervened and separated the two sides. A video of the incident is going viral on social media. Now read the developments in sequence... Several office-bearers and workers, including Samajwadi Party district vice-president Sudhir Dubey and Mukesh Barua, were present at the meeting held at SS Garden in Bijauli village. During the meeting, a discussion began about the PDA Chaupal programme organised in Jaitpur. Sudhir Dubey and Mukesh Barua traded allegations over the programme. They first engaged in a verbal altercation, after which a scuffle broke out between them. As the situation deteriorated, their supporters also confronted each other. The viral video shows supporters of both sides pulling and shoving one another, with the situation appearing to verge on a physical altercation. Workers managed to separate the two sides. Meeting was to discuss strategy for the 7 October protest The Samajwadi Party has proposed a protest outside Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's office on 7 October. The meeting was called to discuss preparations and strategy for the protest. The meeting discussed assigning responsibilities related to the protest to local office-bearers and workers, as well as ensuring the participation of as many workers as possible. During this, an old dispute resurfaced. Mukesh said-there was an argument among workers Mukesh Barua acknowledged that an argument and dispute had taken place among the party workers over the issue. However, he denied having any personal dispute with Sudhir Dubey. Sudhir Dubey, meanwhile, said that there was democracy in the party. He said such exchanges among party workers were normal. He denied that there was any personal dispute. For now, the viral video is being discussed among the party's local workers. Neither leader has acknowledged the matter as a personal dispute.

stories.title: Wife cries holding Subedar husband’s feet:Caresses son’s body, daughter faints crying; 3 funeral processions held together in Deoria
stories.summary: The bodies of the Army subedar, his son, brother and nephew reached Deoria on Monday morning. As all four bodies arrived at their ancestral village, the family was overwhelmed with grief. The subedar's wife clung to her husband's feet and wept uncontrollably. His daughter fainted while crying. After regaining consciousness, she insisted on seeing her father's face and repeatedly ran towards him, but family members restrained and comforted her. The entire village turned out to pay tribute to the subedar. People raised slogans of ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ and ‘May they remain immortal’. When the biers of the subedar, his son and brother were carried out of the house together, the entire village was moved to tears. After a funeral procession covering about 2 km, the bodies reached Baikunth Dham on the banks of the Bathua river in Rudrapur. Meanwhile, the nephew's body was also brought to Baikunth Dham from another village. The last rites of all four will be performed here. The incident took place in Gahila Dudhaiala village, under the jurisdiction of Rudrapur Kotwali, around 22 km from the district headquarters. On Sunday, Gaurav Singh (18), the only son of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh, his brother Ram Samujh (55) and his relative nephew Rajan Singh (35) died in a tragic accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur while bringing back Subedar Major Satyawan Singh's body. See the heartbreaking pictures Understand the entire matter in sequence- Look at the pictures from the accident... Wife seeks ₹5 crore compensation for family Sarojni Devi, the wife of martyred Subedar Satyawan Singh, wrote to DM Madhusudan Hulgi and SP Abhijeet, urging the Chief Minister to provide financial assistance of ₹5 crore to each family. She also demanded the construction of a grand entrance gate in the village in her martyred husband's name and the allocation of a petrol pump in his name. In addition, she appealed for one government job for each family member.

stories.title: Sisters run tea stall to become IAS officers:DM speaks to them over phone, promises all possible help; invites them to his residence
stories.summary: DM Deepak Meena spoke by phone on Sunday with the sisters in Gorakhpur who sell tea to prepare for the IAS examination and buy medicines for their paralysed father. He asked about the family and enquired about their father's condition. He then called them to his residence at 10 a.m. on Monday. The DM assured the sisters that he would provide all possible help. The three sisters run the shop together throughout the day and prepare for the examination on YouTube until 2 a.m. A short while ago, Dainik Bhaskar prominently published the story of the sisters' determination. Following this, the administration has stepped forward to help them. The eldest sister, Vartika Upadhyay, said, We received a call from the DM's office at around 9 p.m. The person speaking said that the DM wanted to meet us. Father paralysed, household responsibilities fall on the sisters Vandita Upadhyay, a resident of Maharajganj, said, I live with my family in a rented house in Bargadwa. My father, Ramsakal Upadhyay, was previously a branch manager at Reliance Life and Insurance Company in Maharajganj. The family's financial condition was stable. In 2017, her father became paralysed. He subsequently lost his job. The family's financial condition began to deteriorate. Her mother, Madhuri, is a housewife. There was no other permanent source of income in the household. Taught tuition and worked jobs, but still could not make ends meet Vandita said that, along with her father's medicines and household expenses, she was also worried about the future of the three sisters. She started tutoring young children and also took up odd jobs. But this was not enough to cover the family's expenses. About four years ago, the three sisters planned to open a tea shop. They thought it would be easy to start a tea stall on a small budget. However, their mother refused. She said, Our relatives are well-off. What will they think if they see us doing this? They will make fun of us. Saved ₹8,000, then opened a tea stall After that, we dropped the idea of opening a tea shop. But the family's financial condition gradually began to deteriorate. The financial strain also affected the education of the elder brother. Twenty-six-year-old Shivam Upadhyay studied up to Class 12, after which he had to discontinue his education. He currently works from home as a telecaller for a company. Four months ago, the three of us sisters revisited our old idea and started a tea stall opposite the DDU gate with ₹8,000. We named our stall Believer Bistro. It felt somewhat strange in the early days because we used to study there. But gradually, everything returned to normal. People started coming, and they liked the taste of our tea. When we began making some profit from the sales, I added Maggi to the menu along with tea. Elder sister Vartika is preparing for the IAS examination. She wants to become a DM in the future. Vandita and Avantika are still in college. As they also run the tea stall throughout the day, they have less time to prepare. However, they do study from 12 midnight to 2 a.m. Vandita wants to join the police department after becoming an IPS officer, while Avantika wants to become an IAS officer. Mother says-daughters are my strength Mother Madhuri says that her daughters have been her strength even during difficult times. Earlier, I was afraid of what people would think and refused to set up a stall, but now I am happy that they are doing their work. Their dream will certainly come true. Father Ramsakal, meanwhile, says that he is proud of his daughters. The way they have managed the entire family without anyone's support over the past few years is no small achievement. I am happy that they are doing for themselves what I could not do for them. They did not lose courage. ₹3 lakh to ₹4 lakh has been spent on treatment Vandita said that at least ₹3 lakh to ₹4 lakh has been spent on her father's treatment so far. More expenses continue to accrue. His medicines cost ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 a month. He was also taken to Nepal for treatment. During this period, all their savings were exhausted. There are a few decimals of farmland in the village, which are looked after by people living nearby.

stories.title: Kanpur govt doctor dies by suicide:Married 3 years ago; shoots himself with licensed revolver at 2 am
stories.summary: A government doctor in Kanpur allegedly died by suicide after shooting himself in the chest with his licensed revolver. His wife rushed into the room after hearing the gunshot and found him lying on the floor in a pool of blood. Family members took Dr Sandeep Singh (47) to Regency Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place around 2am on Sunday at Blossom Apartment in Nirala Nagar. Singh was a surgeon posted at a community health centre in Kanpur Dehat. Singh's father Raj Bahadur said his daughter-in-law Kanchan called him during the night and told him that Sandeep had shot himself and that she was taking him to hospital. DCP Dipendra Nath Chaudhary said the forensic team has seized the revolver. Dr Sandeep lived separately from parents Singh was a resident of Paradevanpurwa in Lal Bangla. His father Raj Bahadur Singh is a retired Army subedar. Sandeep had three brothers — Vishal, Vikram and Rahul. Vishal died after an illness, while Rahul died in a hit-and-run case in Noida. Raj Bahadur lives in Paradevanpurwa with his wife and younger son Vikram. Sandeep lived separately with his wife Kanchan, daughter and two-month-old son at Blossom Apartment in Nirala Nagar. Second marriage took place in 2019 His cousin Mohit said Sandeep's first marriage was in 2007 to Keerti Singh, an MBBS doctor from Kanpur. They had a 12-year-old son and divorced by mutual consent in 2018. Sandeep married Kanchan Singh, a resident of Kasganj, in 2019. Kanchan is a homemaker and they have two children — four-year-old Mahi and a two-month-old son. Raj Bahadur said disputes had started between Sandeep and Kanchan over minor issues soon after their marriage. He would often intervene and try to settle their differences. He said he last spoke to Sandeep around 9.30 pm on Sunday and asked about his well-being. According to the family, Sandeep later had an argument with his wife. Around 2am, he took out his licensed revolver, went to the prayer room, touched Laddu Gopal's feet and then sat before the temple and shot himself in the chest. Completed MS from GSVM Medical College in 2010 His cousin Rishabh Singh said Sandeep completed his MBBS from Jolly Grant Medical College in Dehradun in 2006 and MS from GSVM Medical College in Kanpur in 2010. He then joined Hallet Hospital and worked there for around nine years before being transferred to Kannauj. After working there for six years, he was posted at a CHC in Kanpur Dehat. He had been working there as a general surgeon for the past one-and-a-half years. Kidwai Nagar SHO Neeraj Dwivedi said, The case appeared to be one of suicide by shooting himself in the chest. He said a family dispute had emerged as a possible reason in the preliminary inquiry. The body has been sent for post-mortem, and the exact reason will be clear only after questioning.

stories.summary: The flood situation is worsening in Uttar Pradesh. Ten rivers are in spate after water was released from dams following heavy rainfall in the hills. Despite no rain for the past eight days, 11 districts, including Lucknow and Sitapur, remain affected by floods. In Lucknow, the water level of the Gomti river has been rising rapidly for the seventh consecutive day. Around 40,000 houses in the Faizullaganj area are submerged under 4-5 feet of water, affecting nearly 3 lakh people. Thousands have been forced to leave their homes, while boats are operating on the streets. Amid the floodwaters, a house wall suddenly collapsed. Hanumant Dham, the Lete Hue Hanuman Temple and Chandrika Devi Temple along the Gomti Riverfront have also been submerged. Dozens of villages in Ballia and Gonda have been cut off and turned into islands.
