stories.title: ₹50,000 fine on doctors who beat attendants:Clash breaks out at Gorakhpur’s BRD Medical College
stories.summary: BRD Medical College administration in Gorakhpur has taken strict action over a dispute between patients' attendants and junior doctors at Nehru Hospital. The altercation took place on Tuesday night after the death of a patient injured in a road accident, when the attendants demanded that a post-mortem examination be conducted. Fines ranging from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 have been imposed on the six junior doctors involved in the incident. All six junior doctors have also been suspended for one week. To prevent a recurrence, the college administration has decided that the accused junior doctors will undergo psychiatric counselling every week for one month. They have also been made to submit written affidavits stating that such incidents will not happen again. CCTV footage became the basis of the investigation All six accused junior doctors were summoned before the committee formed to investigate the dispute that took place late on Tuesday night. CCTV footage was also examined during the investigation. Based on the footage, none of the accused was able to deny their role in the incident. A fine of ₹50,000 each has been imposed on the three main accused junior doctors, while the three other junior doctors who supported them have each been fined ₹25,000. All of them have given a written assurance that such an incident will not recur in the future. Accused doctors to undergo counselling The college administration has not limited the matter to punitive action alone. Along with arranging regular counselling for the accused junior doctors, it has also decided to send new students for soft-skills training and counselling sessions. The aim is to prepare doctors to communicate with patients and their attendants and to handle stressful situations more effectively. The junior doctors had also lodged a complaint against the patients' attendants. They alleged that a large number of attendants had gathered in the corridor of the medicine ward and that one attendant had tried to grab and pull a female junior doctor by the hand. They said this was what led to the situation worsening. The college administration has also taken this aspect seriously. Questions have also been raised over the role of the security guard deployed at the time of the incident. The administration has written to the Sainik Welfare Corporation seeking the removal of the guard deployed at the scene. The administration says 15 guards were deployed there. The guard posted at the Medicine Ward gate was responsible for preventing attendants from entering the gallery and calling another guard for help. Victim files complaint against doctors The investigation into the assault on an attendant at BRD Medical College is now proceeding on the basis of a viral video and the complaint filed by the victim. Injured Ajay Singh has filed a complaint with Gulhariya police, making several serious allegations, including assault, against junior doctors and other staff members. He has also provided the police with a video related to the incident. The police are investigating the authenticity of the video and the sequence of events shown in it. According to injured Ajay Singh, a resident of Semra in the Gulhariya area, a dispute broke out over a demand for a post-mortem examination after the death of his relative, Umakant Chaudhary. During the incident, the doctors and staff members closed the channel gate of the gallery in Ward No. 11 and assaulted him. Full details of the case Umakant Chaudhary, a resident of Tenuhारी Soyam village in the Kotwali police station area of Sant Kabir Nagar, was injured in a road accident on 3 October. He was referred to BRD Medical College after receiving primary treatment at the district hospital. At the medical college, he was admitted to Ward 11 of the Medicine Emergency department because of a head injury. He died during treatment at around 12 midnight on Tuesday. According to the attendants, the junior doctors on duty issued a death certificate and told them to take the body home. The attendants demanded a post-mortem because the death had occurred in a road accident. This led to a heated argument between the two sides. Attendants alleged that as the dispute escalated, the channel gate of the gallery in Ward No. 11 was closed and they were assaulted. A video of the incident is going viral on social media. Police brought the situation under control The dispute continued until around 2 a.m. on Tuesday night. On receiving the information, police reached the spot and brought the matter under control after speaking to both sides. A memo was then prepared for the post-mortem and sent to Gulriha police. The medical college administration had formed a three-member committee to investigate the entire matter. Action was taken against the doctors after its report was submitted. In this connection, BRD Medical College Principal Dr Dharmendra Kumar said that the incident was reviewed before the inquiry committee on the basis of CCTV footage. Action has been taken against six junior doctors.

stories.title: Hailstorm in western UP, floods in Lucknow:8 Gonda villages submerged, 13 houses swept away in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: The weather suddenly changed across western Uttar Pradesh on Friday morning. Meerut witnessed heavy rain accompanied by hail. In Muzaffarnagar, hailstones the size of peas fell without any rain. The weather department has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for eight districts today. Meanwhile, floods continue to cause trouble across the state. In Lucknow, the water level of the Gomti river has been rising for the 11th consecutive day. Roads in VIP areas have been submerged. Water has entered several temples, including Lete Hanuman and Hanumant Dham. The Riverfront has been closed until further orders. Water has reached neck level in the lanes of Faizullaganj. More than 40,000 houses are over half submerged, affecting a population of over 3 lakh. The Ghaghara river is in spate in Gonda, with floodwater entering eight villages. More than 7,000 people are stranded in the flood. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda river is causing severe erosion. So far, 13 houses and four temples have been washed away into the river.

stories.title: 6.45 lakh voters removed in Gorakhpur to be verified:BLOs to visit every voter’s home to check current status
stories.summary: After the completion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll, voters who were left out of the final voter list published on 10 April 2026 or whose names were deleted will be verified again. The list published on 7 January 2025, before the SIR, will be compared with it. The names included in the earlier list but missing from the post-SIR list will be verified. Their number is approximately 6,45,000. A booth-level list of all such voters will be given to Booth Level Officers (BLOs), who will visit their homes and verify them. During the verification, the current status of those whose names are missing from the later list will be checked. Those found to be eligible will be asked to fill out Form 6. Verification must be completed within a month The verification campaign will continue for a month. During this period, young people who have turned 18 will also be registered as voters. Within a month, all voters will be verified and a list will be prepared, recording their current status. The names of those who have been made to fill out Form 6 will also be included in this list. It will be shared with representatives of political parties. Camps to be held in homeless and workers' settlements too The campaign will not be limited to door-to-door verification. Camps will be set up at the booth level to add names to the electoral roll. Special camps will be organised for people staying in night shelters, workers' settlements, those who are homeless and those living outside the mainstream of society. Information about the process of getting names added will also be provided through educational institutions, public outreach, SVEEP activities and press briefings. The District Election Officer and Electoral Registration Officer will regularly review and monitor the campaign. How many voters were there before and after SIR? Gorakhpur had more than 36.66 lakh voters before the SIR. The campaign removed more than 6.45 lakh names. A large number of them were people who were voters but could not provide the necessary information or records linked to their own names or those of their parents or grandparents in the 2003 electoral roll. Figures released at the district level after the SIR showed that 6,45,634 names had been removed and that the number of voters had fallen to 30,20,908. During the SIR, providing details of the 2003 records through a declaration form along with Form 6 had become important. The removal of this additional requirement may now provide relief to people who had been getting stuck in the application process because they did not have information about old family records. Chillupar saw the highest number of deletions Constituency-wise, Chillupar saw the highest number of deletions, with 87,732 names removed. It was followed by Bansgaon, where 83,062 names were removed, and Khajni, where 83,014 names were removed. The number of names removed was 70,763 in Gorakhpur Rural, 68,242 in Campierganj, 67,355 in Chauri Chaura, 62,175 in Pipraich, 62,152 in Gorakhpur City and 61,130 in Sahjanwa.

stories.title: 'You’re beautiful, my wife can’t make me happy':Home guard commander accused of rape; woman threatens suicide
stories.summary: A woman in Uttar Pradesh's Jaunpur has accused a Home Guard platoon commander of sexually assaulting her over eight years and threatening to kill her husband and children if she refused to comply. She has alleged that he exploited her financial difficulties and forced her to continue the relationship against her will. “If I do not get justice, I will set myself on fire outside the Chief Minister's residence in Lucknow,” the woman said. She also alleged that the accused was pressuring her to change her statement after she approached the police. The case relates to the Badlapur police station area, around 38 km from the Jaunpur district headquarters. The woman approached the police on October 7, according to the report. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to her over the phone. Woman says accused took advantage of her financial difficulties The accused, Dharmendra Sharma, alias Makrand, 44, lives in Sarokhanpur and works as a Home Guard platoon commander in Badlapur. He lives with his wife, two daughters and a son. The woman lives nearby with her husband and children. The woman said she married in 2017 and was struggling financially after moving to her marital home. Her family owed around ₹3,000 for milk supplied by the accused's household. She said the accused offered her work at his house, promising to pay her ₹12,000 a month. She began looking after livestock and also worked at his house and fields. “I thought that if I found some work, I could help with the household expenses. Dharmendra told me to work at his house and promised to pay me ₹12,000 a month,” she said. She alleged that she worked at his house and fields for three years but was never paid the full amount. 'You look very beautiful': Woman alleges sexual abuse The woman alleged that the accused began making inappropriate remarks and pressuring her to enter into a sexual relationship. “He used to tell me, ‘You look very beautiful. Get into a relationship with me. I will help you,’” she said. She alleged that he exploited her financial circumstances and sexually assaulted her against her will. She said she became pregnant in 2019 as a result of the alleged relationship. The woman said she told her husband that the accused was harassing her. According to her, the accused continued to trouble her, including by entering her house at night. She alleged that when her husband objected, the accused became aggressive and threatened those who intervened. 'He threatened to kill my husband and children' The woman said she eventually asked the accused to leave her alone, but he threatened her family. “When I told him that enough was enough and asked him to leave me alone, he said that if I did not have physical relations with him, he would kill my husband and me,” she alleged. She said she continued to comply because she feared for her husband and children's lives. She also alleged that when she went to her parental home to escape the harassment, the accused threatened to kill her husband if she did not return. “He used to say, ‘I feel satisfied with you. My wife cannot keep me happy. I will stay with you,’” she said. The woman said the accused was married and had two daughters, aged 17 and 18, and a 16-year-old son. Woman alleges accused smashed her phone The woman said she suffered a miscarriage in February this year. Despite her poor health, she alleged, the accused continued to pressure her for sex. She said she had recorded videos to support her account and establish her innocence. When she warned the accused that she had evidence against him and would take it to the police, he allegedly assaulted her and smashed her phone, destroying the recordings. “I had complained against him three times. Every time, he would say that the police station was in his pocket and that I could do nothing against him,” she alleged. The woman said the accused assaulted her again on the night of October 5, prompting her to approach the police. Woman claims she is being pressured to change statement The woman alleged that after she filed the complaint, the accused called village residents and pressured her to change her statement. She also claimed that he took ₹2.85 lakh from a self-help group and had not returned the money. “My husband is also no longer willing to keep me with him after learning everything. If he goes to jail, his family is capable of getting him released immediately. But my children's future and mine have been ruined,” she said. The woman said she had attempted suicide three times in the past and threatened to set herself on fire outside the Chief Minister's residence in Lucknow if she did not get justice. Police say dispute was over money, both parties reached settlement Badlapur police station in-charge Phoolchand Pandey said the dispute was related to a financial transaction. “There was a dispute over a monetary transaction. The woman had lodged a complaint earlier, and a case was registered under those sections. Both parties have now reached a settlement. A final report (FR) will be filed in the FIR case,” Pandey said. The police statement differs from the woman's allegations of prolonged sexual abuse, threats and pressure to withdraw her complaint. The status of the FIR and the proposed final report should be verified before publication.

Bundelkhand gets heavy rain instead of Purvanchal:2-day rain equals monthly quota; drought-hit areas now flooded; 8-year analysis
stories.summary: The pattern of monsoon rainfall in Uttar Pradesh is changing. Until 8 years ago, eastern UP received more rainfall, while western UP and Bundelkhand often received less. But the picture has now changed. Areas that traditionally received less rainfall, such as Mahoba, Jalaun and Banda, are now recording “very heavy rainfall”. Here, the monthly rainfall quota is being met within just 2-4 days. The pattern of rainfall across the state has also changed. This is creating flood-like conditions in some areas and drought-like conditions in others. Dainik Bhaskar analysed 8 years of monsoon rainfall data in UP from 2019 to 2026. The analysis revealed 4 major changes in the rainfall pattern. The biggest change is visible in the difference in rainfall between eastern and western UP. Read the report… First change: Rainfall pattern changed rapidly after 2022 The past 50 years of monsoon rainfall data (LPA) show that eastern UP has received more rainfall than the western part. Eastern UP has received an average of 799.2 mm of rainfall, while Western UP has received 672 mm. However, this pattern appears to have changed over the past 8 years. According to the IMD, eastern UP received 7% more than average rainfall in 2019, at 852.4 mm. In comparison, western UP received only 523.8 mm, which was 20% below average. In 2020, when eastern UP received 2% less rainfall, the rainfall deficit in western UP was 32%. However, in 2022, the two regions were almost at par. After that, the situation gradually reversed. In 2023, western UP came close to normal rainfall with 696.2 mm, while eastern UP remained at 567.3 mm, or 29% below average. In 2024, rainfall in both regions was almost equal. In 2025, western UP received 12% more rainfall than average, while eastern UP received 17% less. In 2026, western UP received 16% more rainfall, while eastern UP received only 2% more. If we look at the figures district-wise, the picture becomes even clearer. Of the 33 districts in western UP, 12 received below-average rainfall, while 25 of the 42 districts in eastern UP faced a rainfall deficit. Second change: Heavy rainfall in traditionally water-deficient Bundelkhand The biggest change is visible in Bundelkhand. Mahoba is the clearest example. The region receives an average of 597.9 mm of rainfall during the monsoon season. In 2019, it received 518.2 mm. However, in 2026, it received 1,127 mm of rainfall, which was 88% above average. Banda has an average rainfall of 767.1 mm. This year, it received 1,348.4 mm, which was 76% above normal. It also received 41% more rainfall in 2025. Chitrakoot received 1,358.1 mm of rainfall, which was 73% above normal. Hamirpur is another example of this change. It receives an average of 708 mm of rainfall. In 2026, it received 1,307.7 mm, which was 85% above normal. Overall, Bundelkhand, which is traditionally associated with low rainfall and drought, is now receiving much more rainfall than average. This trend has been clearly visible since 2022. However, it would be premature to say that the weather in Bundelkhand has permanently changed. Eight years of data is not conclusive evidence of climate change. But it does show that even areas traditionally affected by rainfall deficits are now experiencing very heavy rainfall in some years. Third change: Rainfall decreased in June-July, August-September made up the deficit The timing of the monsoon in UP, meaning how much rainfall the state receives in each month, also appears to be changing. According to an IMD study covering 20 years from 2001-2020, the normal pattern in UP was for July to receive the highest rainfall. On average, around 34% of monsoon rainfall occurred in July and 31% in August. However, the data from 2019 to 2026 shows that the share of August and September is increasing. In 2019, only 40.2 mm of rain was recorded in June. This was followed by 296.9 mm in July, 169.1 mm in August and 213.8 mm in September. This means a large share of the year’s rainfall came after July. The change became more evident from 2022. That year, only 193 mm of rainfall was recorded in June-July, while August-September received 340.5 mm. This means around 64% of the rainfall came in the final two months. In 2023, 52% of the monsoon quota was received in August-September. In 2024, this figure reached 60%. The trend became even stronger in 2026. By July 31, rainfall was 27% below average, and August-September made up the deficit. By the end of the season, UP had recorded 8% more rainfall than average. Over these 8 years, only 2020 and 2025 saw consistent and good rainfall from June to September. The overall indication is that the monsoon appears to be shifting from June-July towards August-September. However, years such as 2020 and 2025 also show a different pattern. Therefore, it would be premature to call this a permanent change in the monsoon pattern. Fourth change: Monthly rainfall quota being met within 2-4 days The way monsoon rainfall occurs in UP is also changing. The number of rainy days is decreasing, while dry spells are increasing. On the other hand, when it does rain, a large amount of water often falls within a short period. This means the number of days on which rainfall is spread across the monsoon season has decreased. But within a few hours or 1-2 days, rainfall equivalent to an entire month can occur. For example: In 2020 and 2021, several districts experienced such intense rainfall an average of 3-5 times, fulfilling 30-50% of their monthly rainfall quota. In 2022, more than 60% of September’s rainfall was received through heavy rain over 2-3 days. In September 2023, there were 3-4 days when western UP and the Terai areas recorded up to 180 mm of heavy rainfall in 24 hours. In 2024 and 2026, several such days were recorded in eastern and western UP when 30-40% of the monthly quota was met in a single day. In September 2026, there were 4-5 such days when up to 245 mm of rainfall was recorded within 24-48 hours. Historically, eastern UP was known for heavy rainfall. However, over the past 8 years, the number of days with heavy rainfall has increased in parts of western UP and Bundelkhand. Due to the changing pattern, the total rainfall figures on paper may appear normal or even above normal, with rainfall crossing 800 mm in 2026. However, this is leading to waterlogging, inadequate groundwater recharge and severe damage to crops.

‘Killed my husband, I should be hanged’:Beautician wife in Meerut confesses; says, ‘I miss him, regret it’
stories.summary: I killed my husband with the help of my lover and his friend. I request the law to give me the death penalty along with both of them. My husband used to fight with me every day. That day too, he strangled me and threatened to kill me. I then called my lover and asked him to come. I mixed a sedative into my husband’s food and gave it to him. My lover came with his friend. I held my husband’s legs, his friend held his hands, and my lover strangled him with a dupatta. I am missing my husband a lot. I regret what I did. I have done wrong. Meerut beautician Ilma made this confession while speaking to Dainik Bhaskar. The incident took place on September 28 in Zakir Nagar Colony under Lohia Nagar police station. After the murder, the family was informed that Talib had died of a heart attack, and they buried his body. However, after the deceased’s mobile phone was found on October 5, the family began suspecting his wife. When they questioned her strictly, she confessed to the murder. On Thursday, the grave was dug up and the body was exhumed and sent for post-mortem. Couple married 4 years ago; they have a 3-year-old daughter Talib (30), son of Zulfiqar from Rasulpur-Dabhedi village in Muzaffarnagar, married Ilma (27), daughter of Momin from Anjum Palace in Meerut’s Brahmapuri area, four years ago. They have a three-year-old daughter. Talib worked as a mason. After their marriage, he lived with his wife in a rented house in Zakir Nagar Colony, Meerut. Ilma worked at the nearby Signature Style Beauty Studio. Now read the accused wife’s full confession They had a fight in the afternoon; husband beat me badly Ilma said, “At around 3:30 pm on September 28, my husband Talib returned home from work. At that time, I had gone to give a facial to the landlord’s son’s wife. Talib called me, and I returned home shortly afterwards. When I reached home, Talib and his nephew Sharik were lying down. Talib asked me to knead the flour and make rotis. After I made the rotis, we had an argument over work. Talib beat me badly, after which I went and sat in another room. After some time, Talib came to call me and we had another argument.” Husband strangled me, so I called my lover Ilma said, “After the argument, I called my lover Aman and told him that Talib was beating me and threatening to kill me. He had also strangled me several times. Aman said over the phone that he was coming and would ‘deal with’ Talib after he arrived. “I then gave Talib food mixed with a sedative. After some time, Aman arrived. He was accompanied by another young man, his friend.” Wife held his legs, friend held his hands, Aman strangled him Ilma said, “Talib was unconscious. Aman’s friend held his hands while I held his legs. Aman then strangled Talib with a dupatta. I had met Aman around 13–14 months ago at 60-Futa crossing. He gave me his number and said he would help me get a job at a parlour. “Talib found out about Aman around 6–7 months ago. After that, they had several arguments and fights over the phone. However, Talib had never met Aman in person. He had only seen him in photographs.” Ilma said, ‘I don’t know what suddenly happened to me’ When Dainik Bhaskar asked Ilma why she broke the trust of her husband and her four-year-old marriage for a relationship that began around 14 months ago, and why she killed him, she said, “I don’t know myself what happened to me. I had no intention of killing my husband beforehand, but suddenly all this happened.” Daughter witnessed the murder Ilma said, “My husband beat me during the argument. He also threatened to hit our daughter. After that, I became even more angry with him. When we were killing my husband, our daughter was using a mobile phone. After the murder, when the dupatta was removed from my husband’s neck, the girl saw all of us. However, she did not say anything. “When asked about her daughter’s future, Ilma said that Talib’s family would look after her. “Nothing is going through my mind about what will happen next. I will accept whatever punishment the law gives me.” Mother said, ‘They got my son-in-law, who was like my own child, killed’ CO said, ‘Further action will be based on the post-mortem report’ Kotwali CO Sangram Singh said, “Talib’s grave was dug up and his body was exhumed in the presence of the administration. SDM Bhupendra Singh and CO Gajendra Singh, along with a large police force, were present during the process. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report.”

stories.title: 11 UP athletes at Asian Games:One learnt javelin with stick, another drove cabs at night; one won ₹3 crore without playing
stories.summary: A total of 85 medals came to India at the Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Of these, 16 medals were won by athletes from UP — 5 gold, 3 silver and 8 bronze. These are not just medals, but the result of the struggles of 11 athletes who achieved success despite difficult circumstances. One athlete could not get a javelin for practice, so he peeled bamboo and made a spear-like javelin himself. Another lost his father, drove a cab in Delhi, supported his family and still brought glory to the country despite difficult circumstances. Let’s take a look at the stories of such athletes… The first story is of Rohit Yadav from Jaunpur. Rohit, who won a bronze medal in javelin throw, began practising not at a sports academy but in the fields of his village. He would help his father with farm work and often throw sticks to measure the distance. Rohit’s father, Sabhajeet Yadav, was himself an athlete. He recognised his son’s talent, but the family’s financial condition was so poor that he could not afford to buy a real javelin for him. Seeing Rohit’s growing passion, his father cut and peeled bamboo growing near their house in 2013 and made javelins for him. What happened next was that 14-year-old Rohit started practising his throws with the bamboo stick itself. Later, after saving money, he bought a javelin. He then began practising javelin throw every day. After 13 years of hard work, he finally reached the Asian Games. In the javelin throw final, he won the bronze medal with a throw of 84.35 metres. The government will now give him ₹75 lakh and a government job. Salman Khan from Amethi won a bronze medal in rowing. Salman is the eldest of four brothers and two sisters. He wanted to join the Indian Army and had started preparing for it at the age of 15. But when he turned 18, he lost his father. The responsibility of supporting the family fell on his shoulders. Salman was forced to go to Delhi to earn a living. He initially did small jobs and later started driving a cab. At night, when he would lie down in bed, he would remember his dream of joining the Indian Army. Salman was not someone who gave up easily. He began waking up at 5 am and practising 1,600-metre runs in a park. Sometimes, he would also run 4–5 kilometres. After persistent efforts, Salman finally joined the Army through the sports quota in 2018. It was here that he got an opportunity to train in rowing. Salman pushed himself so hard that today he has won a bronze medal for the country. Jay Kumar Nagar from Noida won a bronze medal in the 4x400-metre relay. Until 2019, he played kabaddi at the district level. Jay’s father runs a small grocery shop in Dadri. Seeing his son’s interest in sports, he got him enrolled at a sports stadium. With his father’s support, Jay left kabaddi and started running on the athletics track. He continued preparing for the 400-metre race every day. On the strength of seven years of rigorous training, he won a medal at the Asian Games. Jay will now receive ₹75 lakh from the UP government. Meeraj Ahmed Khan from Bulandshahr won a bronze medal in shooting at the age of 50. In the 1990s, Meeraj used to play cricket alongside Virender Sehwag. Both were part of the cricket team of Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia University. By the age of 28, Meeraj had captained the Under-19 team. Meeraj dreamed that whenever he played, his jersey would have the name ‘INDIA’ written on it. But he was unable to make it to the Ranji or national team. Meeraj comes from a landlord family. His father Ilyas Ahmed Khan, brother and uncle were all state-level trap shooters. Around 2003, when his cricket career reached a standstill, he went to Delhi’s Karni Singh Shooting Range with his cousin. There, he saw legendary shooters such as Raja Randhir Singh and Mansher Singh, whose jerseys carried the Indian Tricolour. This was when he found a way to fulfil his dream. He then said goodbye to his first love, cricket, and made shooting his career. Rajkumar from Ghazipur played an important role in helping the Indian team win the gold medal at the Asian Games. However, during the match against Bangladesh, he suffered a fracture in the thumb of his left hand. He could not play in the semi-final and final. However, his team registered a शानदार victory in the final to win gold. It also secured a ticket to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Rajkumar Pal is the youngest of three brothers. His elder brothers Jokhan Pal and Rahul Pal were national-level hockey players. Watching them inspired Rajkumar to take up hockey as well. As a child, Rajkumar would play hockey with a bamboo stick and learn the art of scoring goals from his elder brother. When he was 10, his father, Kalika Pal, suddenly passed away. His elder brother Jokhan wanted to play at the international level, but the responsibility of the family now fell on his shoulders. Therefore, Jokhan handed his hockey stick to Rajkumar. He first took him to Karampur Stadium in Ghazipur and then to Meghbaran Singh Hockey Stadium, where Rajkumar learned the finer aspects of hockey. In 2012, Rajkumar was selected for the SAI Sports Hostel in Lucknow. Then, in 2018, another tragedy struck Rajkumar. His elder brother Jokhan Pal died after an illness. However, Rajkumar’s second brother Rahul and their mother Manraji Devi did not let his morale break. His mother and brother worked as labourers and arranged money for him, allowing Rajkumar to continue working hard. He eventually moved ahead and earned his place in the Indian hockey team. Vipraj will get ₹3 crore without playing, Gulveer to receive the highest reward Barabanki’s Vipraj Nigam is an all-rounder in the Indian cricket team. He was part of the 15-member squad selected for the Asian Games. However, he did not get an opportunity to play in any match during the tournament. Team India defeated Bangladesh in the semi-final. India were scheduled to face Afghanistan in the final, but the match could not be played due to rain. India were subsequently declared winners on the basis of their better ranking. Thus, Team India won the gold medal. As per the rules, every member of the squad is considered part of the victory. Therefore, even without bowling or batting a single ball, Vipraj Nigam will receive ₹3 crore from the UP government. He will also be offered a Class-I officer’s job. Gulveer Singh, a resident of Sirsa village in Aligarh, was UP’s most successful athlete this time. He won 2 silver and 1 bronze medal at the Asian Games. Earlier, Gulveer had also won 1 silver and 1 bronze at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. If the five medals from the two major tournaments are considered together, Gulveer will receive the highest prize money from the UP government ₹5 crore. There was a time when it was difficult for him to arrange money to buy athletics kits and shoes. Today, Gulveer is among the athletes from UP receiving the highest prize money.

stories.title: ‘DM uncle, I can’t talk to Papa, please install tower':5-year-old folds hands in Sonbhadra; walks 1km to make calls
stories.summary: A video of a girl appealing to Sonbhadra DM Charchit Gaud to provide mobile network in her village surfaced at 4 p.m. on Friday. In the video, the girl is seen folding her hands and requesting the DM to make mobile network available in the village. The girl says that her father lives away from home. There is no mobile network in the village, so she is unable to speak to her father properly over the phone. After the video surfaced, officials said the mobile network would be upgraded from 2G to 4G. The matter concerns the Nagwan development block. Now read the full story... The girl seen in the video is named Aanvi Patel. She is a UKG student at Hello Kids School in Robertsganj. Aanvi's entire family lives in Robertsganj. Her father, Vikas Patel, is a teacher at a school in Robertsganj. Her mother, Renu Priya Patel, is a homemaker. During the holidays, the family travels from Robertsganj to their ancestral village, Saraigarh, 60 km away. Aanvi is currently in the village with her family. Because there is no mobile network there, she has difficulty speaking to her father. In view of this problem, Aanvi's family members made the video. In the video, Aanvi is seen folding her hands and appealing to District Magistrate Charchit Gaur to have a mobile network installed in the village. The girl says, "Uncle DM, please arrange for a mobile network in my village, Saraigarh. My father lives away from us, and we are unable to call him. Please, Uncle DM!" 2G network available, preparations now under way for 4G BSNL SDO Dharmendra Kumar Singh said, "On the DM's instructions, a survey has been conducted in Saraigarh village. A 2G network is currently available in the village. Preparations are now under way to upgrade the network to 4G. A letter has been sent to senior officials for this. Work on the project is expected to begin soon." District Magistrate Charchit Gaur said, "A survey is being conducted in Saraigarh village. There is a network problem in rural areas. The problem will be resolved soon."

stories.title: Aradhana Misra becomes UP Congress chief:Ajay Rai removed; Imran Masood made working president, Devendra Nishad and Alok Prasad vice-presidents
stories.summary: Congress leadership has removed Ajay Rai as Uttar Pradesh Congress president and appointed Aradhana Misra, MLA from Pratapgarh’s Rampur Khas seat and leader of the Congress Legislature Party, as the new state unit chief. Saharanpur Congress MP Imran Masood has been appointed working president of the Uttar Pradesh Congress. Aradhana Misra ‘Mona’ is a three-time MLA from Rampur Khas and the leader of the Congress Legislature Party. She is the daughter of senior Congress leader Pramod Tiwari. Active in politics for more than two decades, she has also worked with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during the Congress’ ‘Ladki Hoon, Lad Sakti Hoon’ campaign. The party has appointed Devendra Nishad and Alok Prasad as state vice-presidents. Around three months before the Assembly elections, the Congress has made a major organisational change in its Uttar Pradesh unit. The party has sought to focus on Brahmins, minorities (Muslims), OBCs and Dalits ahead of the Assembly polls. Imran Masood is an aggressive leader, known for outspoken views Imran Masood has a strong hold among Muslim and OBC voters in Saharanpur and adjoining areas. He is known for his sharp and outspoken statements. Despite becoming an MP in 2024 with the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance, Masood has openly spoken about differences within the alliance. He publicly claimed that the Samajwadi Party won 37 seats in 2024 only because of its alliance with the Congress. Masood wants the Congress to finalise an alliance with the Samajwadi Party soon for the 2027 elections. During the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, a controversial remark he made about Narendra Modi made headlines across the country. He was also jailed over the remark. At an election rally, Masood had said that if Narendra Modi tried to turn Uttar Pradesh into Gujarat, his “boti-boti” would be cut into pieces.

stories.title: Teacher says ‘Don’t touch me, I’ll kill you’:School manager misbehaves; arrested in Kushinagar; victim asks, ‘What would you do if this happened to your daughter?’
stories.summary: A school manager in Kushinagar sexually harassed a female teacher and threatened to kill her when she objected. A 5-minute 47-second video linked to the incident has surfaced. In it, the manager can be seen making inappropriate advances towards the teacher and making obscene remarks. In the video, the teacher can be heard warning the manager, "Stay away. Don't touch me. I will kill you." She also says that anyone would understand how it would feel if the same thing happened to their daughter. The incident is said to have taken place on Thursday, 1 October. The manager allegedly called the teacher to his office after school hours on the pretext of preparing her transfer certificate (TC). He then allegedly harassed her. The victim lodged a complaint with the police on Thursday night. The police arrested the accused at around 1 p.m. on Friday. He was sent to jail after being produced in court at 5 p.m. This case concerns The Rainbow Loreto School in Kushinagar. The school, located at Saraswati Chowk in the Ravindranagar police station area, provides education up to class eight. The accused school manager, Dinesh Rai, is a resident of Motichhapar village (Bhiswa) in Ravindra Nagar, Kushinagar. His wife is ill. He has a daughter and a son in the family. Manager said, "My wife is ill; I want to have sexual relations with you" The manager asked the female teacher to have sexual relations with him. During the conversation, he cited his wife's ill health and said, "My wife is ill... so I want to have sexual relations with you." The female teacher objected to what the manager was saying. She questioned how he could speak to her in that manner. In the video, the female teacher can be seen repeatedly telling him to stay away. The manager also appears to be trying to move closer to the woman and touch her. It is being reported that the female teacher recorded the conversation on her mobile phone. Now read the conversation between the school manager and the female teacher Female teacher: Sir, whatever you are doing is wrong. You are taking wrongful advantage of this. You are doing something very wrong. School manager: Wrong? Female teacher: Your mind has become polluted. You are a very dirty-minded man. Don't you have a wife? School manager: She is ill. Female teacher: Then get married again. Would you do things like this? I am also someone's daughter and sister. You cannot do this. How old is your daughter? School manager: She is 18 years old. Female Teacher: What would you do if someone did this to your daughter? Answer me. School Manager: I sit down after eating, which is why I have developed a protruding stomach. Female Teacher: Of course it will, when you do not do any work. Look, sir, it is absolutely not the way you think it is. School Manager: Are you mad? Female Teacher: If you want it that badly, get married again. Tell your wife that we are going to get married again. If you need it so badly, go somewhere else, but do not do this at school. School Manager: I will be disgraced there. Female Teacher: So you will not be disgraced at school? Do you do this with every female member of staff who comes here? Your intentions are not right. After this, the female teacher asks why she was called after school hours. She tells the manager to speak clearly instead of making gestures. Female teacher: Sir, you cannot touch me at all. Absolutely not. School manager: Wait for a while, we only want what is best for you. Female teacher: If I were another girl, I would beat you badly at this moment. Stay away from me. According to the video, the female teacher begins to leave the place. During this, she tells the manager to move away from her and leaves while protesting. Police register case under serious sections According to the police, a case has been registered against the accused, Dinesh Rai, under Sections 75, 115(2) and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). These sections relate to sexual harassment, voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation. Find out what punishment may be imposed- BNS Section 75 (sexual harassment): Depending on the sub-section involved, the punishment may be imprisonment for one to three years and/or a fine. BNS Section 115(2): Imprisonment for up to one year, or a fine of up to ₹10,000, or both. BNS Section 351(3): Threatening someone with serious harm, such as death or grievous injury, is punishable by up to 7 years in prison, a fine, or both.

stories.title: Bodies thrown from moving car after murder in Lucknow:Lured on pretext of showing property; held hostage, ₹50 lakh demanded
stories.summary: The KGMU nursing officer and his friend, who had been missing in Lucknow for five days, had been murdered. The killers called them on the pretext of showing them a property. They then held them hostage and demanded a ransom of ₹50 lakh. When the money was not paid, they killed both men. They then threw the bodies from a moving Thar into the Ghaghra river. The police solved the case on Friday evening, relating to the incident on 28 September. The five accused involved in the murders had held the two friends hostage in separate rooms. To avoid suspicion, they parked Pawan's car in Sitapur. Pawan Kumar Garg was an Assistant Nursing Superintendent. He had gone to view a property with his friend Sachin. The killers strangled Pawan and Sachin with a rope The accused strangled Pawan and Sachin with a rope. To destroy the evidence, they threw the bodies into the Ghaghara river from Chalhari Ghat near Mahmoodabad. Madiyaon police and the Crime Branch (North Zone) have arrested all five accused. The accused have been identified as Nitin Mishra alias W (38), a sweet-shop owner from Lodhauli, Itaunja; auto-rickshaw driver Prakash Singh alias Pुद्दी (24); tea-shop owner Suraj Singh (32); commission-agent's accountant Mohit Singh (26); and Avneesh Kumar Maurya (38) of Ajit Puliya, Mall Road, Itaunja. Police recovered the deceased's gold chains and ring, driving licence (DL), Aadhaar card and photocopies of bank statements from the accused. They also seized the Thar and Hyundai cars used to dispose of the bodies. Land purchase plan turned deadly DCP North Amit Kumar Anand said that during police questioning, the main accused, Nitin Mishra alias W Mahraj, said he already knew Pawan Kumar Garg. Pawan had told him that he had ₹50-60 lakh set aside to buy land. He had asked him to show him a good property. After learning that a large sum of money was involved, Nitin conspired with his associates to carry out a kidnapping and extort ransom. On the night of 27 September, Nitin called Pawan to Bhithouli Crossing. Pawan arrived with his friend Sachin Vishwakarma. The accused took both of them to New Fauji Dhaba in Itaunja, where an argument broke out while they were drinking. Held hostage in a house under construction The accused took both men to Nitin's house under construction in Annamau, held them hostage in separate rooms and demanded a ransom of ₹50 lakh. To mislead the police, Nitin took Pawan's Brezza car from the dhaba and left it parked in Sitapur. Around noon on 28 September, after Pawan refused to pay the money, the accused began fearing that they would be caught. At around 12 noon, the accused strangled Pawan and Sachin with a rope and killed them. At around 5:30 p.m. on 28 September, the accused loaded both bodies into a Thar vehicle, took them to Chalhari Ghat and threw them into the Ghaghra river from the bridge. Missing person report filed on 29 September On 29 September, Pawan's nephew Sanjay Garg, a resident of Keshav Nagar, Madiyaon, reported his uncle missing at the Madiyaon police station. The police then began examining CCTV footage and toll plaza records. On 2 October, a case was registered under Section 140(2) of the BNS on the complaint filed by Pawan's brother, Manoj Kumar, and all five accused were arrested based on information provided by an informant near Bhithouli Tiraha. Pawan had recently sold a plot According to members associated with the KGMU Nursing Association, Pawan Garg had been posted as an assistant nursing superintendent at KGMU since 2011. He was currently posted in the orthopaedics department. He spent most of his time in the operation theatre. He left home on the night of 27 September. A few days earlier, he had sold a plot in the Kalli Paschimi area. Subsequently, reports emerged of a transaction with someone regarding the investment of the proceeds. However, this has not been confirmed. He left home at around 8 p.m. on Sunday, initially saying that he was going to Dubagga. It was learnt that he then travelled towards Madiaon in an Innova car. A property dealer friend was with him. When the friend's brother called to ask about his location, he said that he had reached Prerna Sthal. Subsequently, information emerged that Pawan's location had been detected near the Itaunja crossing at around 11 p.m. The police found his car in CCTV footage from the Itaunja toll plaza, and it was later recovered abandoned in Sitapur. The police are investigating the case from several angles. Had been embroiled in a dispute with his wife for several years Pawan Garg had been embroiled in a dispute with his wife for around 10 years. The two had been living separately. Their son lived with his wife. Around three years ago, the couple began living together following a court order. His wife stayed with him for around a year. During this period, they had another son. After two or three months, a dispute broke out between them again. After that, around two years ago, his wife's family took her with them to Rajasthan. Had also been involved in minor disputes According to people associated with the Nursing Association, complaints about Pawan Garg would also come in from time to time in the department. He was somewhat short-tempered and would often speak his mind openly in the heat of the moment. However, he was sociable and helped others when needed. His relations were also normal at the Nursing Association level. He would regularly have disputes over certain matters while working in the department. Family was originally from Rajasthan Pawan Garg's father previously owned a gold and silver shop in Rajasthan. Later, the family shifted to Uttar Pradesh. Pawan Garg joined KGMU in February 2011. He had been living in Lucknow ever since. His wife is said to be originally from Karauli in Rajasthan. Karauli is also said to be Pawan's native place.

stories.title: Anupriya Patel stays silent on Divya Mittal’s questions:Reviews organisation in Lucknow; says NDA will score hat-trick in 2027
stories.summary: Apna Dal (S) chief Anupriya Patel held an organisation review meeting at the party's camp office in Lucknow on Friday, 2 October. The meeting discussed preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, booth management and strategies to strengthen the organisation. After the meeting, a Bhaskar reporter asked Anupriya Patel about the challenge posed by former IAS officer Divya Mittal. Even after being asked the question nine times, Anupriya did not give a direct answer. She preferred to talk about other issues. Claim of an NDA 'hat-trick' in 2027 Speaking to journalists, Anupriya Patel said that Apna Dal (S) is a strong and reliable ally of the NDA. The NDA will secure a major victory in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, just as it did in 2017 and 2022. She said- Our goal is to form an NDA government in Uttar Pradesh again in 2027. The NDA will have a candidate in every seat, whether the seat is allotted to Apna Dal or to another alliance partner. We will try to ensure the victory of the alliance candidate in every seat. To achieve this, every party worker will work on the ground with full strength. 'Opposition should stop making excuses after defeat' Anupriya Patel took a strong stance over the opposition's repeated questioning of the Election Commission, electoral rolls and the election process. She said that when the opposition loses an election, it tries to blame one institution or another instead of analysing its own failures. Dismissing the Opposition's allegations, he asked directly, "If the country's electoral process is completely tainted and flawed, then let the Opposition explain: whose governments are in power in Kerala, Karnataka, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Himachal Pradesh? When Opposition parties win in these states, the entire electoral process suddenly becomes completely transparent and sound, but when the NDA wins the people's mandate and forms the government, questions begin to be raised about the process. If the Opposition's argument is correct, should the governments of all these states also be dissolved?" He further said that the Opposition had gained some electoral advantage in the 2024 election by creating an atmosphere of lies and confusion, but the people had now understood this tactic. The Opposition would face defeat once again in 2027. 'A 100% strike rate is our sole target' Addressing party office-bearers and workers during the review meeting, the Union minister put forward her views in a highly aggressive yet positive manner. After conducting a detailed review of the organisation, she assigned several important responsibilities to the workers- 1. Resolve to achieve a 100% strike rate: Anupriya Patel gave workers clear instructions that the party's goal in the upcoming election should not merely be to contest, but to ensure the victory of every candidate it fields - a 100% strike rate. She said the main purpose of the organisation's review meetings was to ensure that not the slightest shortcoming remained in its structure. 2. Let the flag fly at every doorstep and hut: Supporting the campaigns announced by the state president, she said, 'The time has come for workers to take the Apna Dal flag in their hands and set out from village to village and street to street. Not a single village or booth in Uttar Pradesh should remain where the Apna Dal flag is not seen flying over a house, doorway or hut. When the party flag is visible everywhere, the workers' morale and confidence will increase many times over.' 3. If opponents attack you, know that you are on the right path: Encouraging the workers, he said that when opponents feel threatened by your existence, they resort to abusive language and criticism out of frustration and desperation. He told the workers, "If you are being targeted from all sides, it simply means that you are at the centre of the entire discussion and are receiving plenty of attention. Learn to enjoy the desperation of your opponents and keep your eyes fixed solely on your goal, like a fish's eye." 4. Pay special attention to maintaining linguistic propriety: He strictly instructed all party workers and the social media team that linguistic propriety must not be violated under any circumstances on public platforms, at meetings or on social media. The party's identity must remain that of a disciplined and positive organisation. Major Announcement of Upcoming Programmes The dates of major programmes to be held in the coming days were also announced to further broaden the party's support base. stories.title: 16-year-old boy goes missing after taking initiation from Sant Premanand:Parents protest outside Vrindavan ashram, plead ‘Give our son back’
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy from Hathras has been missing for three months. His parents and other family members arrived in Vrindavan on Friday. They claim that their son was initiated by Sant Premanand Maharaj at the Kelikunj ashram three months ago. He has not returned home since then. The boy has been identified as Anuj Chaudhary. He is a resident of Baramai Kheda village in Hathras. His family members have been staging a sit-in outside the ashram since 11 a.m. Those taking part include Anuj's father, Rajveer Singh, his mother, grandmother, four sisters, uncle and other villagers. The family members said they would not leave the area outside the ashram until Anuj was found. See 4 pictures from outside the ashram : Father said, "Give me my son back. We will leave from here." Father Rajveer Singh said that Anuj's maternal grandparents' home is in Panigaon, near Vrindavan. During this time, he started visiting Keli Kunj Ashram to seek the blessings of Sant Premanand Maharaj. After some time, he decided to take initiation and, after persuading his mother, received initiation from Premanand Maharaj around three months ago. After taking initiation, he stayed at home for five days. He then said that he was going to seek Maharaj's blessings. He left home carrying the kanthi mala given to him by Premanand Maharaj and three books. Three months have passed since then, but to this day, the family has neither seen his face nor spoken to him. Rajveer Singh said that Anuj is his only son among four daughters. He was studying and was in intermediate this year. He is around 16-17 years old. Rajveer is a farmer. He said, "Give me my son back. We will leave from here." Grandmother alleges: Ashram staff pushed them out Anuj's grandmother, Munni, said, "On the 25th, it had been three months since he received initiation. He came home after receiving initiation. After that, he said he was going to seek Premanand Maharaj's blessings. He went to the Keli Kunj Ashram. Since then, we have received no information about him." She alleged that the family went to the ashram to seek information about Anuj, but the people there did not listen to them and pushed them out. According to Munni, the family also asked to see the recordings from the cameras installed at the ashram, but they were not allowed to check the cameras. Munni said the ashram only told them that Anuj was engaged in spiritual practice and would return. She said the family had filed complaints at the Sadabad and Bisawar police stations. The police also visited the ashram, but the family has still received no information about Anuj. Anuj's grandmother, Munni, said there was still no trace of the child. She said, "There is a saint at the ashram. He told us on Thursday that he would hand over the child within two hours, but there is still no sign of those two hours either. We spoke to him yesterday." According to Munni, the family last spoke to Anuj by phone on the morning of 3. They have been unable to contact him since. She said, "Our only demand is that we want our child. We have not met our child for three months. We have not been sitting here since yesterday, but for three months, yet we still have not been given our child." Police arrive outside the ashram Vrindavan police arrived after receiving information about the sit-in outside the ashram. Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh and Kotwali in-charge Ashwani Kumar spoke to the family members and gathered information about the entire matter. The police team then went inside the ashram and sought information about Anuj. Ashram management says-Anuj is not here A seeker from the ashram came out with the police. He told the family members that Anuj's photograph had been sent to the group of the ashram's volunteers. Thousands of disciples had visited the ashram during Guru Purnima. Information about Anuj was sought at that time as well, but he could not be traced. The ashram management is ready to provide all possible assistance to the family. However, the family members were not satisfied with this response. Case already registered in Sadabad Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh said that a case has been registered in Sadabad in connection with Anuj's disappearance. Records related to his initiation at the ashram are also being checked. Police are investigating the matter. The family alleges that no one from the ashram had been willing to speak to them directly for so many days and that they had not been given clear information about Anuj. -------------------- ... CCTV footage of Premanandji's disciple jumping from the 4th floor: Sat on the boundary for 6 seconds, lay on the floor, then suddenly got up and jumped CCTV footage has emerged showing Premanand Maharaj's 25-year-old disciple, Rasik Dulari Sharan, jumping from the fourth floor in Vrindavan. It shows him sitting on the terrace boundary wall. Six seconds later, he lies down on the floor. He suddenly gets up and jumps over the boundary wall. Seeing this, the second disciple arrives running. He looks down and sees that Rasik Dulari Sharan had died by suicide at 10:35 a.m. on 25 September. stories.title: SP workers, police clash during symbolic ashes procession:Police carry protesters away in Lucknow; SP stages protest
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party workers held a symbolic funeral urn procession for the Election Commission in Lucknow on Friday. Carrying the urn and raising slogans against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft, the workers clashed with police when they were stopped. When police tried to take them into custody, dozens of women and police personnel lay down on the ground. Police officers were seen carrying some protesters by their legs and dragging them towards the van. In one instance, a police officer lifted a worker with both hands, carried him to the van and put him down near it. The police later took the protesters to Eco Garden. The Samajwadi Party workers had gathered near Janpath Market at around 12 noon on Monday and started moving towards the state assembly to protest. However, police stopped them in Hazratganj. The protesters accused the police of misbehaving with them and tearing their clothes. Police tried to stop the protesters at the spot, leading to a long commotion between the two sides. Watch the visuals below : Now read what the activists said... Abhishek Yadav, who had come from Barabanki to take part in the protest, said that Gyanesh Kumar had murdered democracy. "We will remain on the streets until he resigns," he said. He alleged that more than 35 crore votes had been stolen to help form BJP governments in different states and at the Centre. He alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the entire Election Commission, acting at his direction, were working for the BJP. He said they would fight to save democracy, from the streets to Parliament. 'We set out to immerse the Election Commission's ashes' Arriving with an urn containing ashes, Chhotu said they were going to immerse the Election Commission's ashes. They said, "The Election Commission is dead, and this urn contains its ashes." They alleged that the Election Commission was favouring the BJP and that cheating was being carried out continuously. Chhotu alleged that after Bihar and West Bengal, preparations were now under way to influence Uttar Pradesh as well. They said elections would not be allowed to take place in Uttar Pradesh until Gyanesh Kumar was removed as Chief Election Commissioner. According to them, the Election Commission's functioning had weakened democracy. 'The Opposition has been raising the issue of vote theft from the outset' Rinki Singh, who took part in the protest, said that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had been raising the issue of vote theft for a long time. She claimed that evidence had also been presented several times, but the Election Commission had taken no action. Rinki said that questions had once again been raised over the Election Commission's role following a report published in an English newspaper. She alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party was benefiting from the Election Commission's collusion.

stories.title: Ordered wrench, pepper spray online to kill mother:Lucknow son used AI to plan murder in diary; loved dressing like girls
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy was detained by Lucknow police in connection with the murder of his mother on Friday. The investigation found that he had planned the murder in advance. He had ordered a master wrench and pepper spray online and had also written the murder plan in a diary with the help of AI. The diary also contained details of the items to be used in the murder and instructions to keep hot water ready to destroy evidence after the incident. Police have taken the diary, mobile phone, wrench and the clothes worn during the incident into custody and sent them for forensic examination. According to the police investigation, the boy did not like his parents’ restrictions. He would become aggressive when anyone touched his body. He also liked dressing and grooming himself like girls. Police are including these aspects in their investigation. See pictures of the crime scene : Reached home on the pretext of meeting his mother, committed the crime within 15 minutes The incident took place on the night of 1 October in a flat at Vision Apartment. According to the police, the boy had reached home on the pretext of meeting his mother. He told her that he would make tea. The room door then remained closed for around 15 minutes. During this time, he struck his mother several times on the head with a wrench. After the incident, the boy himself called his father and the police to inform them about what had happened. As soon as they received the information, police officers, including DCP West Jitendra Srivastava, reached the spot. The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. The boy began living separately in Ganeshganj four months ago A close family member, Naresh, said the boy had been troubled by his gender identity since he was around 10 or 11 years old. His behaviour began to change as he grew older. After disputes and physical altercations began occurring at home, the family rented a separate flat for him in Ganeshganj around four months ago. He then began living there alone. Father says his son was undergoing treatment According to the boy's father, his son had been receiving treatment at different hospitals for mental health problems. Naka police station in-charge Vivek Chaudhary said the teenager had been taken into police custody and was being questioned. All aspects, including the reason for the murder and the dispute within the family, are being investigated. Naka police station in-charge Vivek Chaudhary said- Information related to the incident may be stored on the mobile phone. However, the accused is not revealing the phone's password. Action is currently being taken.

stories.title: CM Yogi spins charkha on Gandhi Jayanti:Children sing ‘Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye’ in Lucknow; says, 'charkha symbolises self-reliance'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath spun a Charkha at Gandhi Ashram in Lucknow on Gandhi Jayanti. He urged people to follow Mahatma Gandhi’s message of Swadeshi and self-reliance in their daily lives. Children also sang ‘Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye’ during the programme. Yogi said Gandhi led movements peacefully and transformed them into mass movements. He recalled his childhood association with the clothes and charkha at Gandhi Ashram. “The Charkha is not just a charkha; it is a symbol of India’s self-reliance and self-sufficiency,” he said. See the pictures... Swadeshi message turned freedom movement into mass movement The CM said Gandhi’s message of moving from Swadeshi to self-reliance became one of the foundations of India’s freedom movement. He said the freedom struggle, which was initially fragmented, became a mass movement under Gandhi’s leadership. Gandhi also encouraged people to embrace Swadeshi and self-reliance. Yogi urged citizens to make Swadeshi, cleanliness and self-reliance part of their daily lives, saying Gandhi’s messages continue to inspire people. He said the Uttar Pradesh government had announced a 25% discount on khadi products until January 30, 2027, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. He urged people to make khadi part of their lives and respect the skills of artisans, craftsmen and weavers. He said the ‘Local to Global’ approach could provide them with a larger platform. Yogi said Gandhi’s message of self-reliance would form a foundation for Viksit Bharat. Yogi recalls Shastri's simplicity and ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ Yogi also remembered former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, describing him as known for his simplicity and good nature. He said Shastri’s personality was simple yet firm and resilient, and that he demonstrated through his actions what he said. Yogi recalled Shastri’s slogan ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’, saying it became a guiding message for independent India. He said soldiers were protecting the country’s borders while farmers were working hard to meet its food requirements. Shastri’s appeal strengthened the sense of respect for both soldiers and farmers, he added. India self-reliant in food production The Chief Minister said India is now self-reliant in foodgrain production. He said the country can meet the needs of its large population and also has the capacity to supply foodgrains to several other countries. Yogi said soldiers guarding the country’s borders also represent the same resolve that Shastri placed before the nation in 1965. Yogi mentions Swachh Bharat campaign Yogi also referred to Gandhi’s emphasis on cleanliness, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi carried forward the message through the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. He said the campaign laid the foundation for a cleaner and healthier India and also helped raise awareness about women’s dignity.

stories.title: MP Chandrashekhar rides on Fortuner bonnet at high speed:5 cops cling to vehicle; returning from Sambhal
stories.summary: A video has surfaced showing MP Chandrashekhar Azad travelling seated on the bonnet of a speeding Fortuner. In the 15-second video, Azad can be seen sitting on the bonnet and leaning against the front windscreen, while five police personnel are hanging from the car’s doors. Several vehicles from his convoy can also be seen speeding ahead of and behind the Fortuner. However, Azad’s security personnel are seen signalling the other vehicles to slow down. The video is reportedly from September 29 and was recorded while Chandrashekhar was returning from a public meeting in Chandausi, Sambhal. After the video surfaced, the MP issued a clarification on Thursday. Chandrashekhar said, “There was a large crowd in the convoy and a traffic jam was forming. The police were unable to control the crowd. Therefore, I had to violate security protocols, sit on top of the vehicle myself and explain the situation to the people.” Check out the VISUALS below : Read the full story below : Azad Samaj Party national president and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad held a public meeting in Chandausi, Sambhal, on 29 September. Hundreds of supporters were present in the event. It is reported that after leaving Chandausi, the supporters' vehicles began travelling with his convoy. The MP said that the large number of vehicles travelling with his convoy caused a traffic jam on the road. To get the jam cleared, he had to climb onto the vehicle himself and appeal to his supporters to clear the way. On Thursday, MP Chandrashekhar clarified the matter in Bijnor. He said a traffic jam had formed in front of the vehicle after the rally in Chandausi. The police were trying to clear the jam but were unable to move the crowd. The police could not even use batons because of him, as a large number of women were present there. He was forced to climb onto the vehicle to remove them and clear the way. The jam was cleared only after he folded his hands and appealed to the people. He added that he could not tolerate traffic jams on the road putting the lives of his workers at risk. If someone who is ill is on the way to hospital and gets stuck in a traffic jam, their life should not be at risk. SP said-Sambhal police can take action When told that the video was from Bijnor, SP KK Vishnoi said the matter was not from Bijnor district. The video is reportedly from Chandausi.

stories.title: Akash Anand apologises to Mayawati:Says won’t join another party; calls her decision to expel father-in-law right
stories.summary: Akash Anand apologised to his aunt Mayawati on Friday, saying she is his political mentor, inspiration and like a mother to him. He said, "Whatever I have learnt in politics, I have learnt from you. Whatever I have done, I have done under your guidance." He said his silence was misunderstood and led to rumours. "If this has hurt you, I apologise to you for it. I only want the opportunity to serve the party and the mission again under your leadership," he said. Akash wrote on X, “Whatever I have learnt in politics, I have learnt from you. Whatever I have done, I have done under your guidance. My silence was misunderstood. If this has hurt you, I apologise to you for it. I only want the opportunity to serve the party and the mission again under your leadership.” Akash also rejected speculation that he may join another party. He said, “I am not joining any other political party—not today, nor ever. The BSP is not just a party for me; it is my family.” After Akash was expelled from the party, Chandrashekhar and Akhilesh had offered him to join their parties. Since then, there had been speculation that he could join another political party. He said Mayawati was right to expel father-in-law from party Akash said Mayawati’s decision to expel Ashok Siddharth, his father-in-law, from the party and his decision to retire from politics was completely right. “I stand with that decision. Relationships have their place, but the mission is bigger than them. It is my responsibility to put the interests of the party and the movement above personal and family interests,” he said. Akash’s post has led to speculation that Mayawati may take him back into the party. There is also speculation that he could be given an important post ahead of the UP Assembly elections.

stories.title: School bus crash in Kanpur kills woman teacher:3 students injured, glass shards pierce heads and faces; they were heading for Gandhi Jayanti event
stories.summary: A school teacher died and half a dozen people were injured after a speeding dumper collided head-on with a school bus in Kanpur on Friday morning. Three children were among the injured, and two of them were referred to Hallet Hospital in critical condition. The accident took place around 8 a.m. near Harbaspur village on the Kanpur-Sagar Highway. At the time of the accident, 35 people, including five students, were travelling on the bus. The impact was so severe that the bus windows shattered, and broken glass scattered inside the vehicle. The incident triggered panic and screams among those travelling on the bus. The bus was carrying people who were on their way to attend a Gandhi Jayanti programme at China Public School in Ghatampur. After receiving information about the accident, police reached the spot and took the injured to Bidhnu CHC for treatment. Watch the visuals below : Story being updated...

stories.title: Two BHU women professors cheated:Fraudsters took ₹30 lakh promising flats; gave cheque under pressure, bounced twice
stories.summary: Two female professors from Banaras Hindu University (BHU) were duped of ₹30 lakh on the pretext of providing flats in Sunderpur on Friday. They booked one flat each at Brij Enclave but did not receive possession even after the promised deadline. Police have registered an FIR against builder Avinash Upadhyay, his brother Kalindi Upadhyay, Rishikesh Upadhyay and their mother after cheques issued to refund the money bounced. Dr Shabnam, one of the BHU teachers, had also lodged an FIR on September 23. Flats booked in May 2021 According to Dr Rita Singh's complaint, she and Dr Shabnam booked one flat each in a project by Sunderpur-based builder Avinash Upadhyay in May 2021. They each paid ₹15 lakh for the flats. The builder had promised to construct the flats and hand over possession by June 2022. The agreement also stated that if the flats were not handed over within the given period, the entire amount would be refunded with interest. However, the flats were not handed over even after the deadline. Flats booked on second floor still incomplete According to the complaint, both professors had booked flats on the second floor of the building. However, construction of the flats is still incomplete. The complaint alleges that the builder's phone has also been switched off for nearly two years. After considerable pressure, the builder gave both professors cheques for ₹15 lakh each, but the cheques bounced when deposited in the bank. About a month later, the builder issued cheques again, but bounced again. Chitaipur police have registered an FIR against four people, including the builder, and started an investigation. Station House Officer Rakesh Gautam said the documents related to the case were being examined. Further action will be taken based on the allegations in the complaint and the transaction documents.

stories.title: ‘Akhilesh divorced us, we accepted’:Minister Rajbhar calls SP sinking boat; says ‘Those who want to die can go there’
stories.summary: Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar lashed out at SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, saying, “Akhilesh Yadav has divorced us. We have accepted it too. We said, ‘Accepted, accepted, accepted’ three times. Why are you shouting now? The SP is a sinking boat; whoever wants to die should go there.” Rajbhar made the remarks on Friday in response to Akhilesh Yadav’s statement during a press conference on Thursday. Akhilesh had said, “You bring Rajbhar to us, and we will take him. We are waiting. He won with the SP’s votes; how will he win on his own again?” Rajbhar said, “What regard is there for party workers in the Samajwadi Party? Is any leader valued there? Muslims are treated as slaves there. The extremely backward classes are treated as slaves there. The party is dominated by the family, criminals and wealthy people.” He also targeted the SP’s PDA formula, saying that until recently the party talked about PDA — backward classes, Dalits and minorities. He said that now the family and wealthy people such as Dhanraj and Parimal Nathwani had entered the picture. Rajbhar added that the party was now looking for a criminal so that it could complete its PDA formula. Mayawati also lashes out at Akhilesh, saying, PDA is just a sham; tickets go to family members and wealthy businessmen Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati targeted Akhilesh Yadav over giving a ticket to Dhanraj Parmal Nathwani. She posted on X on Friday morning, saying, "The SP's PDA and socialism are a sham. Akhilesh has fielded his relative Ram Gopal Yadav in the Rajya Sabha election. The second candidate is Dhanraj Parmal Nathwani, who comes from a major industrial house." "The third candidate is only for face-saving. The SP needs PDA votes, but wants to make family members and capitalists MPs and MLAs. This is the SP's double standard. The poor, Dalits, Adivasis, extremely backward classes, Muslims and minority communities should become aware before the election. Their interests are safe only in the Ambedkarite BSP; everything else is a deception." About Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, whom Akhilesh gave a ticket
